# DataTable

## Purpose

Sortable data table on TanStack Table that renders cards below a width threshold, with optional row press, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: @tanstack/react-table, react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/data/DataTable
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { DataTable } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/data/DataTable";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { DataTable } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/data/DataTable";`

### Dependencies

- `@tanstack/react-table` (`createSortedRowModel`, `flexRender`, `rowSortingFeature`, `sortFns`, `tableFeatures`, `useTable`): optional peer, `^9.0.0`.
- `react-native`: `FlatList`, `Pressable`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `View`.
- `zustand`, `zustand/vanilla`: optional peer.
- `../styles.ts`: `joinClasses`. `./table-layout.ts`: `dataTableLayout`, `tableContentWidth`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (data)
Import count: 0

`DataTableProps<T extends RowData> extends Omit<ViewProps,"children">`. Read: `onLayout`, `style`, `accessibilityLabel` (defaults to "Data table"). The rest is forwarded to the root `View`. `TronColumnDef<T>` is `ColumnDef<typeof features, T, unknown>` from `@tanstack/react-table`; the features are row sorting only.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `readonly T[]` | none | yes | Copied with `[...data]` into `useTable`. |
| `columns` | `TronColumnDef<T>[]` | none | yes |  |
| `getRowId` | `(row: T) => string` | none | no | Passed to `useTable` only when set. |
| `onRowPress` | `(row: T) => void` | none | no | Makes rows `Pressable` buttons with hint "Opens this record". |
| `width` | `number` | none | no | Overrides the measured width. |
| `layout` | `DataTableLayout` | "auto" | no | See Variants. |
| `cardsBelow` | `number` | 620 | no | Width under which `auto` gives cards. |
| `minColumnWidth` | `number` | 144 | no | Used for the content width of the table layout. |
| `getColumnLabel` | `(columnId: string) => string` | none | no | Takes priority over a string header, then the column id. |
| `renderCard` | `(row: Row<typeof features, T>) => ReactNode` | none | no | Replaces the default card. |
| `rowHeight` | `number` | 44 | no | Row `minHeight` (table) and empty-state height. |
| `headerHeight` | `number` | 44 | no | Header `minHeight`. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | 640 | no | Root `style.maxHeight`. |
| `emptyLabel` | `string` | "No records" | no |  |
| `sortable` | `boolean` | true | no |  |
| `className` | `string` | none | no | Joined onto the root classes. |
| `headerClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `rowClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `cellClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | false | no | Drops the built-in classes. |

### Tokens

`node tokenuse.mjs` output:
- `space.2` from `gap: 8` (x1)
- `space.1.5` from `paddingVertical: 6` (x2)
- `space.2.5` from `gap: 10` (x1)
- `space.3` from `paddingHorizontal: 12` (x2)
- `color.text` (x1), `color.border` (x4), `color.surfaceRaised` (x2), `color.textMuted` (x1), `color.surfaceSunken` (x2), `color.focus` (x2)
- `radius.card` (x1), `radius.control` (x1)
- `minWidth: 0`: no token (x1)

Tailwind default classes (no token): `gap-3` (x2), `p-4`, `border` (x12), `min-w-0` (x3), `min-h-11`, `gap-2`, `px-3` (x3), `flex-row`, `flex-1`, `w-full`, `items-center`, `justify-center`, `ring-2`. Also unmapped literals: `width: "40%"`, `fontWeight: "600"`.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: whether the example's column types check against the real `@tanstack/react-table` 9 API. The check harness has a TanStack version that lacks `useTable`, `tableFeatures` and related exports, so `check.sh` reports errors inside `DataTable.tsx` itself and `TronColumnDef` may resolve loosely. None are reported under `examples/DataTable.tsx`.
- UNVERIFIED: screen reader announcements for the sort buttons and row buttons; no assistive technology was run.

## Variants

`layout` resolves through `dataTableLayout`:
- `"cards"` and `"table"` are used as given.
- `"auto"`: `"cards"` when the width is `null` (before measurement) or below `cardsBelow`, else `"table"`.
- Cards: optional horizontal sort-button strip, then a `FlatList` of cards (`gap-3 p-4`, plus `rounded-card border border-border bg-surface-raised` when styled).
- Table: horizontal `ScrollView`, header row, `FlatList` of rows; column area width is `max(width, columns x minColumnWidth)`.
- An unknown `layout` string, a `cardsBelow` that is not above 0, or a negative width throws `RangeError`.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `empty` | derived in code | `ListEmptyComponent` shows `emptyLabel` in both layouts. |
| `sorted` | derived in code | a header or sort button carries `accessibilityValue.text` of "sorted ascending", "sorted descending" or "not sorted", plus an arrow glyph hidden from accessibility. |
| `pressable row` | derived in code | `onRowPress` set gives `accessibilityRole="button"`; unset gives `disabled` on the row `Pressable`. |
| `focus` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | sort buttons carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` (styled). |
| `unstyled` | `unstyled` prop | removes the surface, border and text-colour classes. |

No loading, error or hover code.

### Motion

none in source

### Platform notes

none in source

## A11y

- Contrast: text-text on surface-raised 17.79/13.83:1; header band bg-surface-sunken with text-text 16.01/15.31:1; row separators border-border 1.58/1.58:1, decorative.
- Keyboard and focus: Sortable headers carry `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-focus` (focus/surfaceRaised 5.81/6.93:1, focus/surfaceSunken 5.22/7.67:1) (:148, :195). Body rows have no focus style and are focusable only when onRowPress is set (Pressable disabled otherwise). Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Sort buttons min-h-11 (:147), headerHeight and rowHeight default 44 (:54, a prop, size.touch). Android: 44 below 48 (F08). Card mode rows are a Pressable around the card. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: Wide mode (:181-231) is Views and Pressables with no table, row, cell or columnheader role anywhere (roles appear only at :142 :164 :190 :210 as button or header). The root has accessibilityLabel="Data table" but no role (:127). A row Pressable is an accessible element on iOS, so its cells merge into one announcement. Column and row relationships are lost (F01).
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **FAIL**. Wide layout exposes no table structure (1.3.1, 4.1.2).
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=DataTable
import { DataTable, type TronColumnDef } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/data/DataTable";

type Row = { id: string; name: string; status: string };
const columns: TronColumnDef<Row>[] = [
  { accessorKey: "name", header: "Name" },
  { accessorKey: "status", header: "Status" },
];
const data: Row[] = [
  { id: "a", name: "Gateway", status: "Online" },
  { id: "b", name: "Relay", status: "Offline" },
];

export const Example = () => (
  <DataTable<Row> data={data} columns={columns} getRowId={row => row.id}
    onRowPress={row => console.log(row.id)} layout="auto" cardsBelow={620} />
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `getRowId` when rows have stable ids, since it is forwarded to `useTable` only when set.
- Set `layout` to `cards` or `table` when the breakpoint must not depend on measured width, because `auto` falls back to `cards` before the first measurement.
- Set `onRowPress` only on rows that open a record, since it turns them into buttons with the hint "Opens this record".

### Don't

- Do not ship the wide `table` layout as an accessible table, because the a11y review is FAIL with no table, row or columnheader role (F01).
- Do not pass a `cardsBelow` of 0 or less, an unknown `layout` string or a negative `width`, because each throws a RangeError.
- Do not treat announcements for the sort buttons and `onRowPress` row buttons as verified, because the page marks them UNVERIFIED.

| `expandedIds` | `readonly string[]` | none | no | Controlled expansion. |
| `defaultExpandedIds` | `readonly string[]` | [] | no | Initial uncontrolled expansion. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(next: readonly string[]) => void` | none | no |  |
| `selectedIds` | `readonly string[]` | none | no | Controlled selection. |
| `defaultSelectedIds` | `readonly string[]` | [] | no |  |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(next: readonly string[]) => void` | none | no | Per the comment: taps, Space and Shift range. |
| `columnOrder` | `readonly string[]` | none | no | Controlled order. |
| `onColumnOrderChange` | `(next: readonly string[]) => void` | none | no | Called by the header "Move left/right" accessibility actions. |
| `pinnedColumnIds` | `readonly string[]` | none | no | Passed to `orderTreeColumns`. |
| `renderCell` | `(node: TreeGridNode, column: TreeGridColumn) => ReactNode` | none | no | Falls back to `String(node.values?.[column.id] ?? "")` in a `Text`. |
| `compactBelow` | `number` | 620 | no | Measured width under which the compact layout is used. |
| `rowHeight` | `number` | 48 | no | Row `minHeight` (compact: `rowHeight + 44`) and the height estimate. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | 640 | no | `FlatList` `maxHeight`. |
| `emptyLabel` | `string` | "No items" | no |  |
| `className` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | false | no |  |

`TreeGridColumn` (same file): `id: string` (required), `title: string` (required), `width?: number` (cells use 140 when unset).

`TreeGridNode` (data/tree-grid.ts): `id: string`, `label: string`, `values?: Readonly<Record<string, string|number|boolean|null>>`, `children?: readonly TreeGridNode[]`.

### Tokens

`node tokenuse.mjs` output:
- `space.2` from `gap: 8` (x1), `space.1` from `paddingVertical: 4` (x1), `space.3` from `padding: 12` (x1)
- `<Component>.space.11` from `paddingLeft: 44` (x2; component-scoped pattern, not a global token)
- `size.touch` from `minHeight: 44` (x3) and `minWidth: 44` (x2)
- `color.text` (x1), `color.textMuted` (x1), `color.surfaceRaised` (x1), `color.focus` (x3), `color.border` (x2), `color.primary` (x2), `color.surfaceSunken` (x2)
- `radius.control` (x1)

Tailwind default classes (no token): `rounded-control` (x1), `border` (x6), `min-w-0` (x1), `ring-2`, `border-b`. Unmapped literals include `width: 224`, `height: 44`, `paddingLeft: min(depth*16,128)`, default column width 140.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: which keys `treeGridKey` handles and what each does; only its call site in `TreeGrid.tsx` and its exports list were read.
- UNVERIFIED: runtime behaviour of the `role="row"`, `role="cell"` and `role="columnheader"` mapping on Android, iOS and web; only the source comment states intent.
- UNVERIFIED: that the pinned strip stays aligned during native-driver scrolling; no device was run.

## Variants

- Wide layout (`width >= compactBelow`, where `width` starts at 0 until layout): a horizontal `Animated.ScrollView`, a sticky header row, and rows with a pinned strip (label plus pinned columns, translated by the scroll offset) beside scrolling cells. The label column is 224 wide.
- Compact layout (`width < compactBelow`; this is also the layout before the first measurement): the header row is omitted; each row stacks the label over cells that show their column title at `42%` width.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `expanded` | derived in code | a row with children has a button labelled "Expand <label>" or "Collapse <label>" with `accessibilityState.expanded`; the row has `aria-expanded`. Glyphs "▾" and "▸". |
| `selected` | derived in code | `aria-selected` on the row; `bg-primary/10` (styled); label `fontWeight: "700"`. |
| `focused` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | internal `focusId`; `ring-2 ring-focus` on the row and the pinned strip (styled). The toggle button also carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus`. |
| `empty` | derived in code | `ListEmptyComponent` shows `emptyLabel`. |
| `Keyboard` | derived in code | `onKeyDown` forwards `key` and `shiftKey` to `treeGridKey`; if it returns a result the event is prevented, and a focus move scrolls with `scrollToIndex`. |

- controlled and uncontrolled expansion, selection and column order, each chosen by whether the matching prop is `undefined`.
No loading, error or disabled code.

### Motion

- `Animated.Value` `scrollX` is fed by `Animated.event` with `useNativeDriver: true` on the horizontal scroller (`scrollEventThrottle={16}`) and applied as `translateX` to the pinned header and pinned row strips.
- `scrollToIndex` and `scrollToOffset` use `animated: false`.
- `scrollX` is reset to 0 when leaving the compact layout.

### Platform notes

Only a comment: rows and cells use `role` rather than `accessibilityRole` because "row" and "cell" are absent from Android's `AccessibilityRole` enum and would throw there. No `Platform.OS` checks or sibling files.

## A11y

- Contrast: text-text on surface-raised 17.79/13.83:1. Selected row bg-primary/10 against the raised surface is 1.15/1.2:1 (F04). Focused row adds ring-2 ring-focus 5.81/6.93:1.
- Keyboard and focus: role=treegrid, focusable, onKeyDown with roving focusId (:208-213); the focused row shows ring-2 ring-focus (:188). Expand button has its own ring (:161). Web keyboard path present. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Expand button minWidth and minHeight 44 (:162, size.touch); row label minHeight 44 (:155); header height 44 (:223). Compact data cells minHeight 28 are not interactive. Android: 44 (F08). Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: treegrid, row (aria-selected, aria-expanded), columnheader, cell, expand button with Expand/Collapse label and expanded state, leaf spacer hidden (:141-209). Uses role not accessibilityRole for row and cell on purpose (Android enum). Column reorder exposed as accessibilityActions.
- Motion: Animated.Value scrollX drives the pinned-column offset from the user's scroll (:73, :220). It tracks input, so no reduce-motion issue.
- Review status: **FAIL**. A selected row that is not focused is marked only by a tint at 1.15/1.2:1 (1.4.11).
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=TreeGrid
import { TreeGrid, type TreeGridColumn } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/data/TreeGrid";

const columns: TreeGridColumn[] = [
  { id: "size", title: "Size", width: 96 },
  { id: "kind", title: "Kind" },
];

export const Example = () => (
  <TreeGrid
    columns={columns}
    pinnedColumnIds={["size"]}
    defaultExpandedIds={["src"]}
    onSelectionChange={ids => console.log(ids)}
    nodes={[
      { id: "src", label: "src", values: { size: "12 KB", kind: "folder" }, children: [
        { id: "index", label: "index.ts", values: { size: "2 KB", kind: "file" } },
      ] },
      { id: "readme", label: "README.md", values: { size: "1 KB", kind: "file" } },
    ]}
  />
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `expandedIds` with `onExpandedChange` to control expansion, because each of the three state groups is controlled only when the matching prop is not `undefined`.
- Provide `renderCell` for non-string values, since the fallback renders `String(node.values?.[column.id] ?? "")`.
- Set `compactBelow` to the width where columns stop fitting, because narrower layouts drop the header and stack label over cells.

### Don't

- Do not rely on the selected row tint alone, because `bg-primary/10` measures 1.15:1 against the raised surface (F04) and the review is FAIL (1.4.11).
- Do not assume `treeGridKey` key handling is documented, because the page marks which keys it handles as UNVERIFIED.
- Do not trust `pinnedColumnIds` alignment during native-driver scrolling, because the page marks it UNVERIFIED.

# Badge

## Purpose

Small status badge with neutral, info, success, danger or accent tone, a status dot and size steps, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/feedback/Badge
```

- Import: `import { Badge } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/Badge";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { Badge } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/Badge";`

### Dependencies

- `joinClasses` from `../styles.ts`.
- react-native (peer, required): Text, View.
- No optional peers.

## Props

| `tone` | `BadgeTone` | `"neutral"` | no |  |

| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |

### Tokens

### Unverified

none

## Variants

`tone`:
- `neutral`: `bg-surface-sunken`, label `text-text-muted`, no dot.
- `info`, `success`, `danger`, `accent`: `bg-surface-raised`, label `text-text`, plus a dot View with `border-info`/`border-success`/`border-danger`/`border-accent`, `style={{borderWidth:3}}`, `h-1.5 w-1.5 rounded-full`.

`size`:
- `xs`: root `gap-1 px-1.5 py-0.5`, label `text-xs leading-4`.

none in source.

Label is 12pt (text-xs), text threshold 4.5:1 applies and passes.
- Keyboard and focus: Static, not focusable.
- Touch target: Not interactive.
- Screen reader: accessible with accessibilityLabel = label (:40). Tone is carried by the dot and by the label text, never by colour alone. The dot is aria-hidden.
- Motion: None.

## Example

```tsx example=Badge
import { Badge } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/Badge";

  return <Badge label="Draft" tone="info" size="xs" />;
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Choose `tone` of `info`, `success`, `danger` or `accent` when status matters, since each adds a dot and `text-text` label rather than relying on color alone.
- Use `size` of `xs` for dense rows, which tightens padding to `px-1.5 py-0.5`.
- Write a short, self-describing `label`, since it is both the visible text and the `accessibilityLabel`.

### Don't

- Do not add `onPress` behaviour to a `Badge`, because it is static and not focusable per the a11y review.
- Do not set `unstyled` and expect the tone dot, because the dot and `tone` classes come with the built-in styling.

# Banner

## Purpose

Inline status banner with info, success, danger or neutral tone, title, description, action slot and dismiss button, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/feedback/Banner
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.

### Tarball install

## Variants

`tone` class strings: `info` `border-info bg-surface-raised`; `success` `border-success bg-surface-raised`; `danger` `border-danger bg-surface-raised`; `neutral` `border-border bg-surface-sunken`. Styled root also has `gap-3 rounded-card border ps-4 py-3` and `pe-1` with `onDismiss`, else `pe-4`.

|---|---|---|

| `close hover/pressed/focus` | class `hover:bg-surface-sunken active:opacity-70 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | `hover:bg-surface-sunken active:opacity-70 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus`. |

`active:opacity-70` on the close control. No Animated calls.

### Platform notes

none in source.

## A11y

## Example

```tsx example=Banner
import { Banner } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/Banner";
import { Button } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/Button";

export function SaveFailed({ retry, close }: { retry: () => void; close: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Banner
      tone="danger"
      live="alert"
      title="Could not save"
      description="Check your connection and try again."
      action={<Button title="Try again" variant="secondary" onPress={retry} />}
      onDismiss={close}
      dismissLabel="Dismiss message"
    />
  );
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `live` to `alert` only for urgent failures, because it maps to an assertive live region while the default `status` is polite.
- Pass `onDismiss` to render the close button, and set `dismissLabel` when "Dismiss" is not specific enough.
- Always supply `tone` and `title`, since both are required and the title carries the meaning.

### Don't

- Do not assume the announcement is verified on every platform, because the page marks `role="alert"` and `status` behaviour on native as UNVERIFIED.
- Do not omit `tone`, because it is required and has no default.
- Do not rely on `ps-4`, `pe-1` and `pe-4` spacing without checking your Tailwind setup, because the page marks logical-property support UNVERIFIED.

# EmptyState

## Purpose

Empty-list placeholder with heading title, description, icon or illustration, and an action or secondary exit button, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: @nyc-tron/Button

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/feedback/EmptyState
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { EmptyState } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/EmptyState";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { EmptyState } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/EmptyState";`

### Dependencies

- `Button` from `../Button.tsx` (subpath `./components/Button`); `joinClasses`.
- react-native (peer, required): Text, View.
- No optional peers.

## Props

`EmptyStateProps` extends `Omit<ViewProps,"children">`.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">`

| `exitAction` | `EmptyStateExit` | none | no | Rendered as `Button variant="secondary"`. |

| `illustration` | `ReactNode` | none | no |  |

| `tone` | `string` | none | no | Accepted and discarded (`_tone`). |

`EmptyStateExit`:

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | `string` | none | yes | Button title. |
| onPress | `()=>void` | none | yes |  |
| accessibilityHint | `string` | none | no |  |

### Tokens

- `color.text` x1, `color.textMuted` x1

Tailwind default classes (no token): `gap-2`, `px-6`, `py-8`, `text-base`, `font-semibold`, `text-sm`, `max-w-sm`, `mb-2`, `mt-3`, `leading-6`, `leading-5`, `text-center`.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: How `role="heading"` with `aria-level` is exposed on iOS and Android: the file's own comment says native announces a heading without a level.

## Variants

## States

Static. The exit control is a `Button` with its own states.

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

none in source.

## A11y

- Contrast: text-text and text-text-muted on the page surface 17.79/13.83:1 / 6.16/7.14:1.
- Keyboard and focus: Action is a Button (see Button).
- Touch target: Action Button: see Button. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: Title role=heading with aria-level on web (:61). The art slot is caller-owned (comment :28). accessibilityHint is forwarded to the action.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **PASS**. Heading semantics and passing text contrast.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=EmptyState
import { EmptyState } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/EmptyState";

export function NoLayers({ add }: { add: () => void }) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      title="No layers yet"
      description="Add a layer from the toolbar."
      titleLevel={3}
      exitAction={{ title: "Add layer", onPress: add, accessibilityHint: "Creates an empty layer" }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `titleLevel` to match the page outline, since it is passed as `aria-level` and defaults to 2.
- Use `exitAction` for a single secondary escape, because it renders a `Button variant="secondary"` with an optional `accessibilityHint`.
- Pass `illustration` when you have art, since `icon` is ignored when it is given.

### Don't

- Do not pass both `action` and `exitAction` expecting two buttons, because `action` takes precedence.
- Do not pass `tone` expecting a visual change, because it is accepted and discarded.
- Do not treat the heading level as verified on native, because the page marks `role="heading"` with `aria-level` exposure UNVERIFIED.

# ErrorMessage

## Purpose

Inline error text with a danger glyph, announced as an alert; renders nothing when the message is empty, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/feedback/ErrorMessage
```

- Import: `import { ErrorMessage } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/ErrorMessage";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { ErrorMessage } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/ErrorMessage";`

### Dependencies

- `StatusGlyph` from `./glyphs.tsx`; `joinClasses`.
- react-native (peer, required): Text, View.
- No optional peers.

## Props

`ErrorMessageProps` extends `Omit<ViewProps,"children">`. Returns `null` when `message` is falsy.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | `string` | none | no | Nothing renders without it. |
| `surface` | `"page" \| "night"` | none | no | Accepted and discarded (`_surface`). |
| `className` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `messageClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |

### Tokens

- `StatusGlyph` in glyphs.tsx adds `bg-danger border-danger` (separate file, not counted).

Tailwind default classes (no token): `gap-2`, `min-w-0`, `text-sm`, `leading-5`, `pt-px`.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: Whether a live region on a Text mounted with the message is announced on first render: platform behaviour, not shown by code.

## Variants

none.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | derived in code | any non-empty `message`; Text `role="alert"`, `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`, `text-danger`, leading `StatusGlyph tone="danger"`. |
| `empty` | derived in code | no message returns `null`. |

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

none in source.

## A11y

- Contrast: text-danger on raised 6.57/7.24:1, on sunken 5.91/8.01:1. The "!" mark is not the only signal, the text is.
- Keyboard and focus: Static.
- Touch target: Not interactive.
- Screen reader: Text role=alert with accessibilityLiveRegion polite (:33). Both are set, so assertive (alert) and polite differ by platform; neither drops the message.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **PASS**. Announced as an alert, contrast above 4.5:1.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=ErrorMessage
import { ErrorMessage } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/feedback/ErrorMessage";

export function FormError({ message }: { message?: string }) {
  return <ErrorMessage message={message} surface="page" />;
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `message` only when an error exists, because a falsy value returns `null` and renders nothing.
- Rely on the built-in `role="alert"` with `text-danger` at 6.57:1, since the text carries the signal and the glyph is not the only cue.

### Don't

- Do not pass `surface` expecting a theme change, because it is accepted and discarded.
- Do not claim the `message` is announced on first mount, because the page marks live region behaviour for a Text mounted with it as UNVERIFIED.

## Variants

- Precision mode while dragging (`state.mode`, from vertical travel): `fine`, `normal`, `coarse`. The mode name is shown as text only; `precision.ts` defines the thresholds (28 px) and step scales (fine 0.1, coarse 4 in `scrubValue`).
- `forcedColors`: the scale and fill use `CanvasText` and `Highlight` through CSS variables with `forcedColorAdjust:"none"`, and the class strings `bg-border`/`bg-accent` are dropped.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `default, hovered, focused, active (dragging)` | derived in code | scale border class is `border-accent` when active, else `border-focus` when focused, else `border-text-muted` when hovered, else `border-border`; the scale background is `bg-surface-raised` when active, else `bg-surface-sunken`. |
| `editing` | derived in code | the number field's wrapper border is `border-focus`. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` prop | `disabled` prop; root opacity 0.5, buttons and field `disabled`/`editable=false`, `aria-disabled`. |
| `pending` | derived in code | `state.pending` also blocks the control (same disabled treatment, without the 0.5 opacity). |
| `error` | derived in code | `state.error` shows `text-danger` text with `accessibilityLiveRegion="assertive"`. |
| `pressed` | derived in code | no code. |

- active hint text shows the mode label; idle shows `idleHint`.

### Motion

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS==="web"`: `userSelect:"none"` on the scale; `forcedColors` takes effect; `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow` always set.
- Off web, those three aria range props are set only when `min`, `max` and the preview value are all integers; the in-source comment says Fabric and React Native Windows mis-parse non-integer `accessibilityValue`. `aria-valuetext` always carries the exact value.
- Imports `useEditorBoundary` from `gestures/editor-interaction-scope.ts` and `PanResponderDrag` from `gestures/`.
- package.json export conditions: `types`, `react-native`, `default`. No `.native`/`.web` siblings.

## A11y

- Contrast: Label text-text and unit text-text-muted 17.79/13.83:1 / 6.16/7.14:1; error text-danger 6.57/7.24:1. Ticks and rail take scaleColor and accentColor from the caller, or bg-border 1.58/1.58:1 (:181-185); ticks use opacity 0.55 for minor marks. Forced-colors branch uses CanvasText and Highlight.
- Keyboard and focus: Focus tracked in store (:163-164); keyboard handler onKeyDown with focusable={!blocked} (:116, :157). Step buttons are Pressables. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: targetSize default 44 with RangeError under 44 (:76-78, size.touch); step buttons and rail use it (:126-177). Android: 44 (F08). Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: Scrubber: accessibilityRole=adjustable, label, hint copy.gestureHint, aria-valuemin/max/now/text, accessibilityActions increment and decrement (:165-172). Step buttons: role button, label. Error: accessibilityLiveRegion assertive.
- Motion: No animation in the file.
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. Rail and tick contrast depend on caller colours and a bg-border fallback at 1.58/1.58:1 (F15).
  - UNVERIFIED: Rail, tick and focus contrast with the real scaleColor and accentColor (F15). Test: Render the scrubber with the app theme, sample tick, rail and focus pixels against the surface, or run contrast.mjs with the consumer's tokens.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.


## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `min`, `max` and `step` with `max` above `min` and `step` above 0, since all three are required for the range.
- Return a promise from `onCommit` for async saves, because the control is disabled while it is pending and a rejection shows its message.
- Pass `scaleColor` and `accentColor` checked against your surface, since rail and tick contrast depends on them (F15).

### Don't

- Do not pass a blank `label`, a bad `scope` or a bad `revision`, because the identity check throws `RangeError('Invalid scrubber identity')`.
- Do not set `targetSize` below 44 or non-finite, because it throws a RangeError.
- Do not rely on the default `bg-border` rail at 1.58:1 as accessible, because the review is UNVERIFIED on rail and tick contrast (F15).

# PropertyInspector

## Purpose

Form built from a field list of number, choice, boolean and text properties, committing one change at a time, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/Button, @nyc-tron/Select, @nyc-tron/feedback/ErrorMessage, @nyc-tron/shell/UnitInput

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/forge/inputs/PropertyInspector
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { PropertyInspector } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/forge/inputs/PropertyInspector";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { PropertyInspector } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/forge/inputs/PropertyInspector";`

### Dependencies

- `../../shell/UnitInput.tsx`, `../../Select.tsx`, `../../Button.tsx`, `../../feedback/ErrorMessage.tsx`, `../../gestures/editor-interaction-scope.ts`, `./useScopedControl.ts` (which uses `../../shell/useOwnedAction.ts`).
- External: `react`, `react-native`, `zustand`, `zustand/vanilla` (optional peer).

## Props

Exports: `PropertyInspector`, `PropertyInspectorProps`, `InspectorProperty`, `PropertyValue`, `validateInspectorFields`.

`PropertyInspectorProps` extends `Omit<ViewProps,"children">` and `ScopedControlProps` (`scope?`, `revision?`, `disabledReason?`). `style` is appended after `{gap:10,minWidth:0}`; `accessibilityLabel` is set to `label` after the spread.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, 'children'>, ScopedControlProps`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | none | yes | Non-blank, at most 1024 characters. Header text and accessible name. |
| `fields` | `readonly InspectorProperty[]` | none | yes | Up to 128, unique ids. |
| `onCommit` | `(id: string, value: PropertyValue, signal?: AbortSignal) => unknown` | none | yes |  |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |

### Inherited props this component reads

Documented by hand from the source. They come from the extended type, so they are not in the table above.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scope | `string` | `'property-inspector'` | no | Non-blank, at most 512. |
| revision | `string \| number` | `0` | no |  |
| disabledReason | `string` | none | no | Disables every field and shows the text as an error. |

`PropertyValue`: `number | string | boolean`.
`InspectorProperty` always has `id`, `label`, `disabledReason?`, plus one of:
| kind | extra fields |
|---|---|
| `'number'` | `value`, `min`, `max`, `step` (required), `unit?`, `integer?` |
| `'choice'` | `value:string`, `choices:readonly {id;label;disabled?}[]` |
| `'boolean'` | `value:boolean` |
| `'text'` | `value:string`, `maxLength:number`, `multiline?:boolean` |

`validateInspectorFields(fields)` throws `RangeError` for more than 128 fields or duplicate ids; blank or over-long ids (256) or labels (1024); a number with non-finite value, min, max or step, `min>=max`, `step<=0`, a value outside the range, or a non-integer when `integer`; a text `maxLength` that is not an integer from 1 to 65536, or a value longer than it; a choice list over 512 entries, duplicate choice ids, or blank or over-long choice ids (512) or labels (1024). The component also rejects a commit value of the wrong type, out of range or not in the enabled choices with `RangeError('Property value is unavailable')`.

### Tokens

- Colour classes: `color.text` 3, `color.textMuted` 1, `color.border` 1. Radius class: `radius.control` 1.
- Literals: `gap: 10` to `space.2.5` (1), `gap: 4` to `space.1` (1), `gap: 6` to `space.1.5` (1), `padding: 8` to `space.2` (1), `minHeight: 44` to `size.touch` (1).
- no token: `minWidth: 0` (1).
- Tailwind default classes (no token): `border` 3, `rounded-control` 1.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: how `Select` renders its options and disabled option; `Select.tsx` was not read.
- UNVERIFIED: abort-signal and pending semantics of `useOwnedAction` and `useScopedControl` beyond what the call sites show.
- UNVERIFIED: that `Button`'s `accessibilityState={{checked}}` is announced as a toggle.

## Variants

Field `kind` picks the control: `number` renders `UnitInput` (label gets ` (unit)` appended, `min`, `max`, `step` forwarded); `choice` renders `Select` (a missing current value is appended as a disabled "Unavailable: <value>" option); `boolean` renders a secondary `Button` titled "<label>: on|off" with `accessibilityState={{checked}}`; `text` renders a `TextInput` and an "Apply <label>" `Button`.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | derived in code | a pending commit, `disabledReason`, or a field's own `disabledReason` disables that control. A field `disabledReason` also shows under the field in `text-text-muted`. |
| `empty choice list` | derived in code | the `Select` is disabled. |
| `text dirty` | derived in code | the Apply button is disabled until the draft differs from `field.value`. |
| `error` | derived in code | `ErrorMessage` at the bottom shows the commit error or `disabledReason`. |
| `pending` | derived in code | `guard.pending` disables all controls. |
| `hover, focus, pressed` | derived in code | no code here (inherited from children). |

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

none in source. package.json export conditions: `types`, `react-native`, `default`. No `.native`/`.web` siblings.

## A11y

- Contrast: Renders UnitInput, Select, Button, TextInput. Number fields inherit UnitInput's boundary 1.42/1.75:1 (F03).
- Keyboard and focus: Fields are native controls. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Inherits UnitInput 44 and Select 48; multiline TextInput has no minHeight (:43). Android: see parts. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: Root View has accessibilityLabel but no role (:32), so the label is dropped by most screen readers. Header uses accessibilityRole=header; each TextInput has accessibilityLabel (:43).
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **FAIL**. Inherits UnitInput and Select field-boundary failures (F03).
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=PropertyInspector
import {PropertyInspector,type InspectorProperty} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/forge/inputs/PropertyInspector";
const fields:readonly InspectorProperty[]=[
  {id:"w",label:"Width",kind:"number",value:100,min:0,max:1000,step:1,unit:"px"},
  {id:"blend",label:"Blend",kind:"choice",value:"normal",choices:[{id:"normal",label:"Normal"},{id:"multiply",label:"Multiply"}]},
  {id:"vis",label:"Visible",kind:"boolean",value:true},
  {id:"name",label:"Name",kind:"text",value:"Layer 1",maxLength:64},
];
export const Example = () => <PropertyInspector label="Layer properties" scope="layer-1" fields={fields} onCommit={async(_id,_value,_signal)=>{}}/>;
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Give every entry in `fields` a unique `id`, since duplicate ids throw and the maximum is 128 fields.
- Set `disabledReason` to explain why editing is locked, because it disables every field and shows the text as an error.
- Set `min`, `max` and `step` on number fields with `min` below `max`, since `validateInspectorFields` rejects anything else.

### Don't

- Do not rely on the root `accessibilityLabel` as the group name, because the root has no role and the review is FAIL (F03).
- Do not pass a number `value` outside `min` and `max`, or a non-integer when `integer` is set, because validation throws a RangeError.
- Do not claim `Button` `accessibilityState` announces as a toggle for boolean fields, because the page marks it UNVERIFIED.

Rest spread goes to `Pressable`. `accessibilityLabel` reads `rest.accessibilityLabel ?? label`; `accessibilityState` merges `rest.accessibilityState` with `disabled` and, when toggling, `checked`; `style` is appended after the component's own style array.

| `quiet` | `boolean` | `false` | no | No outline while off. |
| `styled` | `boolean` | `true` | no | Class strings off when false. |
| `className` | `string` | none | no |  |

**Glyphs.** All take `styled:boolean` (required) and an optional `size:number`; all render `pointerEvents="none"` views.

| Component | Extra props | Size default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| PlayGlyph | `flip?:boolean` (default `false`) | 14 | Right-pointing triangle; `flip` mirrors it. |
| PauseGlyph | none | 14 | Two bars. |
| SkipGlyph | `back?:boolean` (`false`), `double?:boolean` (`false`) | 12 | Bar plus one or two triangles. |
| PlusGlyph | none | 14 | Two crossed bars. |
| ChevronGlyph | `open?:boolean` (`false`) | 8 | Rotated 45 degrees when open, -45 otherwise. |
| CloseMark | none | 14 | Two rotated bars. |

`OFFICE_TOUCH_TARGET` is `44`. `officeKey(e:OfficeKeyEvent)` returns `{key,shift,mod,alt}`, reading `nativeEvent` first and the event itself second; `mod` is true for `metaKey` or `ctrlKey`. `OfficeKeyEvent` is the parameter type of `PressableProps["onKeyDown"]`.

### Tokens

- Colour classes: `color.text` 5, `color.accent` 3, `color.textMuted` 2, `color.focus` 1, `color.border` 1. Radius class: `radius.control` 1.
- Literals: `gap: 6` to `space.1.5` (1), `gap: 1` to `space.0.25` (1), `borderRadius: 1` to `radius.1` (7), `borderRightWidth: 1.5` and `borderBottomWidth: 1.5` to `border.1_5` (1 each), `opacity 0.45` to `opacity.0_45` (1).
- no token: the `OFFICE_TOUCH_TARGET` 44 minimum width and height, `paddingHorizontal: 10`, glyph sizes and bar widths.
- Tailwind default classes (no token): `rounded-control` 1, `border` 8, `text-sm` 1. The glyphs use `bg-text`, `bg-text-muted` and `border-text-muted` strings.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: how screen readers announce `togglebutton` with `checked` of true, false and `"mixed"` on each platform.
- UNVERIFIED: that `transformOrigin` and the half-clipped triangle in `PlayGlyph` draw the same shape on every host.
- UNVERIFIED: key values `officeKey` receives from native key events; only the two lookup paths are in source.

## Variants

- `ToolButton` `checked`: `true` gives `border-accent bg-accent/10`; `"mixed"` gives `border-accent` with no fill; with `quiet` and not checked, `border-transparent`; otherwise `border-border`.
- `ToolButton` role: `accessibilityRole` is `"button"` when `checked` is undefined and `"togglebutton"` otherwise.
- Glyph shape props listed above (`flip`, `back`, `double`, `open`).

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |

| `ToolButton on` | derived in code | `checked===true`; mixed: `checked==="mixed"`; both set `accessibilityState.checked`; web also sets `role="button"` and `aria-pressed`. |

- Glyphs have no states.

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS==="web"` with `checked` defined: `ToolButton` adds `role:"button"` and `aria-pressed` (comment: web has no togglebutton role). Native uses the `togglebutton` accessibility role.
- `PlayGlyph` uses `transformOrigin:"left"` in a style object; support by host is not stated in the file.
- package.json export conditions: `types`, `react-native`, `default`. No `.native`/`.web` siblings.

## A11y

- Contrast: ToolButton on state: border-accent 5.17/8.86:1 with bg-accent/10; off: border-border 1.58/1.58:1, the icon or label carries identity. Glyph strokes bg-text 17.79/13.83:1.

- Screen reader: accessibilityRole=button, or togglebutton with accessibilityState.checked including "mixed" (:54-56); web gets role=button with aria-pressed (:53). Label defaults to the label prop; iconOnly keeps it.

## Example

```tsx example=office-controls
import {View} from "react-native";
import {ToolButton,PlayGlyph,PauseGlyph,SkipGlyph,PlusGlyph,ChevronGlyph,CloseMark} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/forge/office/office-controls";
export const Example = () => <View style={{flexDirection:"row"}}>
  <ToolButton label="Play" iconOnly checked={false} onPress={()=>{}}><PlayGlyph styled/></ToolButton>
  <ToolButton label="Pause" iconOnly><PauseGlyph styled/></ToolButton>
  <ToolButton label="Next" iconOnly quiet><SkipGlyph styled double/></ToolButton>
  <ToolButton label="Add slide" checked="mixed"><PlusGlyph styled/></ToolButton>
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `checked` to `"mixed"` for partial selections, since it sets `accessibilityState.checked` and uses the `togglebutton` role.
- Set `iconOnly` with a clear `label`, because the label stays as the accessible name while the text is hidden.
- Use `OFFICE_TOUCH_TARGET` (44) when you size neighbouring controls, so hit areas match `ToolButton`.

### Don't

- Do not leave `checked` undefined on a toggle, because `undefined` makes a plain `button` with no pressed state.
- Do not claim how screen readers announce `togglebutton` states, because the page marks it UNVERIFIED.
- Do not assume `PlayGlyph` draws identically on every host, because the `transformOrigin` clipping is UNVERIFIED.

# PanResponderDrag

## Purpose

Single-touch drag transport on React Native PanResponder, no gesture-handler dependency, for React Native and web.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/gestures/PanResponderDrag
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { PanResponderDrag } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/gestures/PanResponderDrag";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { PanResponderDrag } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/gestures/PanResponderDrag";`

### Dependencies

- `react`: `cloneElement`, `useMemo`, `useRef`.
- `react-native`: `PanResponder`.
- `./drag-transport.ts` (types), `./pan-responder-config.ts` (`panResponderDragConfig`).
- Alternative transport named in the comment: `GestureHandlerDrag` (uses `react-native-gesture-handler`, an optional peer); not imported here.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R4 imported by 13 files
Import count: 13

`PanResponderDrag(props: DragTransportProps)`. `DragTransportProps` is defined in `gestures/drag-transport.ts`.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| children | ReactElement | none | yes | One host view; the responder's `panHandlers` are merged into it with `cloneElement`. |
| disabled | boolean | none | no | When truthy, `onStartShouldSetPanResponder` returns false. |
| onBegin | (point: DragPoint) => void | none | yes | On grant. |
| onMove | (point: DragPoint, touches: number) => void | none | yes | `touches` is `numberActiveTouches`. |
| onRelease | (point: DragPoint) => void | none | yes |  |
| onCancel | () => void | none | yes | On termination, or when a start event has other than one touch. |

`DragPoint`: `x: number`, `y: number`, taken from `nativeEvent.pageX` and `pageY`.

### Tokens

`node tokenuse.mjs` output: none.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: how React Native Web and each native platform deliver `pageX` and `pageY` and `numberActiveTouches`; no runtime was run.
- UNVERIFIED: whether `cloneElement` with `panHandlers` replaces responder handlers already set on the child; React's merge rule is not source in this repo.

## Variants

none

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | derived in code | `disabled` stops a drag from starting (it is read at event time through a `latest` ref). |
| `single touch required` | derived in code | a drag starts only when `touches.length === 1`; a start event with a different count calls `onCancel`. |
| `granted drag` | derived in code | `onPanResponderTerminationRequest` always returns false, so a parent responder cannot take it. |

No visual states; the component renders only its child.

### Motion

none in source

### Platform notes

none in source. The doc comment says it works on web and native without an extra dependency and that apps already mounting `GestureHandlerRootView` should prefer `GestureHandlerDrag`.

## A11y

- Contrast: Renders no visuals.
- Keyboard and focus: Adds responder handlers to its child; not focusable.
- Touch target: Not a control.
- Screen reader: None needed; clones the child with pan handlers.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **PASS**. Transport with no UI; the child owns accessibility (see DragGrabHandle, PaneSplitter).
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=PanResponderDrag
import { View } from "react-native";
import { PanResponderDrag } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/gestures/PanResponderDrag";

export const Example = () => (
  <PanResponderDrag
    onBegin={point => console.log("begin", point.x, point.y)}
    onMove={(point, touches) => console.log(point.x, point.y, touches)}
    onRelease={point => console.log("release", point.x, point.y)}
    onCancel={() => console.log("cancel")}>
    <View style={{ width: 48, height: 48 }} />
  </PanResponderDrag>
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass exactly one host view as `children`, since the pan handlers are merged into it with `cloneElement`.
- Handle `onCancel` to clear state, because it fires on termination or when a start event has other than one touch.
- Set `disabled` to block drags, since it is read at event time and makes `onStartShouldSetPanResponder` return false.

### Don't

- Do not expect a parent responder to take over a drag, because `onPanResponderTerminationRequest` always returns false once granted.
- Do not assume `cloneElement` replaces responder handlers already set on the child, because the page marks that UNVERIFIED.
- Do not rely on `pageX` and `pageY` values matching across platforms, because delivery is UNVERIFIED.

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `minWidth` on each `AdaptiveColumns.Item` to the narrowest usable column, since it becomes `flexBasis` and drives wrapping.

### Don't

- Do not omit `gap`, or pass a negative or non-finite value, because it is required and throws a RangeError.
- Do not pass a `minWidth` of 0 or less, because the item throws a RangeError unless it is above 0.
- Do not promise exact wrap points for a given `minWidth`, because they come from the layout engine and the page marks them UNVERIFIED.

# Row

## Purpose

Horizontal flex View with the same token-keyed gap, padding, align, justify and wrap as Stack, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: @nyc-tron/layout/Stack

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/layout/Row
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { Row } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Row";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { Row } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Row";`

### Dependencies

- `react-native`: `View`.
- `StackProps` (type only) from `./Stack.tsx` and `stackStyle` from `./stack-style.ts`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (layout)
Import count: 0

`RowProps` is `StackProps`: same fields, same defaults. The only difference is `flexDirection: "row"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| children | `ReactNode` | none | no | Rendered inside the `View`. |
| gap | `StackSpace` | `2` | no | Key of `space`. `space[gap]` px between children, 8 for the default. Set through the RN `gap` style. |
| padding | `StackSpace` | none | no | Key of `space`. Sets `padding`. |
| paddingX | `StackSpace` | none | no | Key of `space`. Sets `paddingHorizontal`. |
| paddingY | `StackSpace` | none | no | Key of `space`. Sets `paddingVertical`. |
| align | `"flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` | none | no | Sets `alignItems`. Unset leaves the View default. |
| justify | `"flex-start" \| "flex-end" \| "center" \| "space-between" \| "space-around" \| "space-evenly"` | none | no | Sets `justifyContent`. |
| wrap | `boolean` | `false` | no | `true` sets `flexWrap: "wrap"`. |
| className | `string` | none | no | Forwarded to the `View` as `className`. Declared on the interface, so it is read here and passed back explicitly. |
| style | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | none | no | Placed after the built-in style, so it wins. |

### Tokens

- `space.0` to `space.4`: `gap`, `padding`, `paddingX` and `paddingY` are looked up in `space` by key, so `token-use.mjs` does not list them (computed values).

Tailwind default classes (no token): none.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: how the `gap` style resolves on React Native Web and on the Windows, macOS and QNX hosts; no runtime was run.
- UNVERIFIED: whether `className` reaches the `View` on every host; it depends on the consumer's Tailwind or Uniwind interop, which this file does not check.

## Variants

none

## States

None. Row has no interactive or conditional state. `flexDirection: "row"` follows the reading direction, so the first child sits at the start edge in both left-to-right and right-to-left layouts.

### Motion

none in source

### Platform notes

none in source

## A11y

- Contrast: No colour.
- Keyboard and focus: Not interactive. `flexDirection: "row"` keeps source order, so reading and focus order follow child order.
- Touch target: Not interactive.
- Screen reader: Layout only. Sets no role, label or `accessible` prop.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **PASS**. Pure layout.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=Row
import { Text } from "react-native";
import { Row } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Row";

export const Example = () => (
  <Row gap={2} align="center" justify="space-between" paddingX={3}>
    <Text>Volume</Text>
    <Text>80</Text>
  </Row>
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Use `Row` with `Spacer` `flex` to push one child to the far end, since `justify` alone cannot split a group.
- Set `wrap` for chip or tag lists, because `flexWrap` then moves children to the next line.
- Use `paddingX` and `paddingY` instead of `padding` when the two axes differ.

### Don't

- Do not hard-code left and right, because `Row` follows the reading direction and `start` flips in right-to-left layouts.
- Do not nest a `Row` inside a `Row` only to add spacing; set `gap` on the outer one.
- Do not rely on `gap` with `wrap` spacing lines the same on every host, because the page marks the `gap` behaviour UNVERIFIED.

# Spacer

## Purpose

Empty View with a fixed length from the space scale, or flex to fill free space on the main axis, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: @nyc-tron/layout/Stack

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/layout/Spacer
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { Spacer } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Spacer";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { Spacer } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Spacer";`

### Dependencies

- `react-native`: `View`, `ViewProps`.
- `space` from `../../tokens.ts`; `StackSpace` (type only) from `./Stack.tsx`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (layout)
Import count: 0

`SpacerProps` is `Omit<ViewProps, "children"> & SpacerSize`. `SpacerSize` is a union: pass `size`, or pass `flex`, never both. Every other `ViewProps` field is forwarded to the `View`. A Spacer takes no children.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| size | `StackSpace` | none | yes, unless `flex` | Key of `space`. Sets `flexBasis` to `space[size]` with `flexGrow: 0` and `flexShrink: 0`, so it is a fixed length on the parent's main axis. |
| flex | `true` | none | yes, unless `size` | Sets `flexGrow: 1` and `flexShrink: 1`, so it takes the free space on the parent's main axis and pushes siblings apart. |
| style | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | none | no | Placed after the built-in style, so it wins. |

### Tokens

- `space.0` to `space.4`: `size` is looked up in `space` by key, so `token-use.mjs` does not list it (computed value).

Tailwind default classes (no token): none.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: that `flexBasis` sets the length on the main axis the same way in every host layout engine, in a Stack and in a Row; no runtime was run.

## Variants

`size` and `flex` are mutually exclusive in the type.
- `size`: fixed length, one of the `space` keys.
- `flex`: flexible length.

## States

None. The component has no interactive or conditional state.

### Motion

none in source

### Platform notes

none in source

## A11y

- Contrast: No colour.
- Keyboard and focus: Not interactive.
- Touch target: Not interactive.
- Screen reader: Empty View. Sets no role, label or `accessible` prop.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **PASS**. Pure layout.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=Spacer
import { Text } from "react-native";
import { Row } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Row";
import { Spacer } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Spacer";

export const Example = () => (
  <Row align="center">
    <Text>Title</Text>
    <Spacer flex />
    <Text>Edit</Text>
    <Spacer size={2} />
    <Text>Share</Text>
  </Row>
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `size` as a `space` key for a fixed gap that differs from the parent `gap`, since it sets `flexBasis` on the parent's main axis.
- Use `flex` to fill the free space between two groups in a `Row`.

### Don't

- Do not pass `size` and `flex` together, because the type rejects it.
- Do not give a `Spacer` children, because its props omit `children`.
- Do not use it for padding around content; use `padding` on `Stack` or `Row`.

# Stack

## Purpose

Vertical flex View with token-keyed gap, padding, align, justify and wrap, no role and no colour, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/layout/Stack
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { Stack } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Stack";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { Stack } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Stack";`

### Dependencies

- `react-native`: `View`, `ViewProps`.
- `space` from `../../tokens.ts` and `stackStyle` from `./stack-style.ts`, which imports the `StackProps` type from `./Stack.tsx`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (layout)
Import count: 0

`StackProps extends Omit<ViewProps, "children">`. Every other `ViewProps` field, `testID` and the `accessibility*` props included, is forwarded to the `View`.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | none | no | Rendered inside the `View`. |
| `gap` | `StackSpace` | `2` | no | Key of `space`. `space[gap]` px between children, 8 for the default. Set through the RN `gap` style. |
| `padding` | `StackSpace` | none | no | Key of `space`. Sets `padding`. |
| `paddingX` | `StackSpace` | none | no | Key of `space`. Sets `paddingHorizontal`. |
| `paddingY` | `StackSpace` | none | no | Key of `space`. Sets `paddingVertical`. |
| `align` | `StackAlign` | none | no | Sets `alignItems`. Unset leaves the View default. |
| `justify` | `StackJustify` | none | no | Sets `justifyContent`. |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | no | `true` sets `flexWrap: "wrap"`. |
| `className` | `string` | none | no | Forwarded to the `View` as `className`. Declared on the interface, so it is read here and passed back explicitly. |

### Inherited props this component reads

Documented by hand from the source. They come from the extended type, so they are not in the table above.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| style | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | none | no | Placed after the built-in style, so it wins. |

### Tokens

- `space.0` to `space.4`: `gap`, `padding`, `paddingX` and `paddingY` are looked up in `space` by key, so `token-use.mjs` does not list them (computed values). Keys: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4.

Tailwind default classes (no token): none.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: how the `gap` style resolves on React Native Web and on the Windows, macOS and QNX hosts; no runtime was run.
- UNVERIFIED: whether `className` reaches the `View` on every host; it depends on the consumer's Tailwind or Uniwind interop, which this file does not check.

## Variants

none

## States

None. The component has no interactive or conditional state. A `StackSpace` key that is not in `space` is a compile error, not a runtime one.

### Motion

none in source

### Platform notes

none in source

## A11y

- Contrast: No colour.
- Keyboard and focus: Not interactive.
- Touch target: Not interactive.
- Screen reader: Layout only. Sets no role, label or `accessible` prop; `testID` and `accessibility*` props pass through to the View.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **PASS**. Pure layout.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=Stack
import { Text } from "react-native";
import { Stack } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Stack";

export const Example = () => (
  <Stack gap={3} padding={4} align="stretch" testID="settings-stack">
    <Text>Account</Text>
    <Text>Notifications</Text>
  </Stack>
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `gap` as a `space` key such as `3`, since a raw pixel value does not compile and the key keeps spacing on the 4 px unit.
- Set `align` to `stretch` or `center` when children differ in width, because it maps straight to `alignItems`.
- Put your own `style` last in the prop list, since it is applied after the built-in style and wins on any field.

### Don't

- Do not expect a role or a label from `Stack`, because it renders a plain `View`; set `accessibilityRole` yourself when a group needs one.
- Do not rely on `className` reaching the `View` on every host; the page marks that UNVERIFIED because it depends on the consumer's interop.
- Do not leave `gap` unset and assume zero, because it defaults to `2`, which is 8 px.

# Text

## Purpose

Text with body or caption size from the token scale, a font-size override and a theme colour tone, no weight, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/layout/Text
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { Text } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Text";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { Text } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Text";`

### Dependencies

- `react-native`: `Text` (imported as `NativeText`), `TextProps`, `TextStyle`.
- `font` and `leading` from `../../tokens.ts`; `joinClasses` from `../styles.ts`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (layout)
Import count: 0

`TextProps extends Omit<TextProps (react-native), "children">`. The component reads `children`, `variant`, `size`, `tone`, `className` and `style`; every other React Native `Text` prop, `testID`, `numberOfLines` and the `accessibility*` props included, is forwarded.

Extends: `Omit<NativeTextProps, "children">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | none | no | Rendered inside the React Native `Text`. |
| `variant` | `TextVariant` | none | no | Font size and line height from the token scale. Omit it to inherit the size from the parent. |
| `size` | `TextSize` | none | no | Key of `font` (10 to 17). Sets `fontSize` only and replaces the variant, so the variant line height is dropped. |
| `tone` | `TextTone` | `"text"` | no | Theme colour role, as a class (see Variants). |
| `className` | `string` | none | no | Appended after the tone class. |

### Inherited props this component reads

Documented by hand from the source. They come from the extended type, so they are not in the table above.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| style | `StyleProp<TextStyle>` | none | no | Placed after the built-in style, so it wins. |

### Tokens

- `font.11`, `font.12`, `leading.14`, `leading.16`: the two variants. `size` looks up `font` by key, so any `font.10` to `font.17` can be reached (computed, not listed by `token-use.mjs`).
- `color.text`, `color.textMuted`, `color.danger`, `color.primary`, `color.accent`, `color.info`, `color.success`, `color.onPrimary`, `color.onDanger`: one tone class each.

Tailwind default classes (no token): none.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: whether the tone classes paint on every host; they depend on the consumer's Tailwind or Uniwind interop and on the consumer defining the matching CSS variables.
- UNVERIFIED: how a fixed `lineHeight` behaves under the system font scale on each host; no runtime was run.

## Variants

### variant

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `body` | `fontSize: font[12]`, `lineHeight: leading[16]`. |
| `caption` | `fontSize: font[11]`, `lineHeight: leading[14]`. |

Those are the two size and line height pairs that occur three or more times in `ui`. There is no weight and no font family: Text does not set `fontWeight` or `fontFamily`.

### tone

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `text` | `text-text`. |
| `muted` | `text-text-muted`. |
| `danger` | `text-danger`. |
| `primary` | `text-primary`. |
| `accent` | `text-accent`. |
| `info` | `text-info`. |
| `success` | `text-success`. |
| `onPrimary` | `text-on-primary`. |
| `onDanger` | `text-on-danger`. |

The default tone `text` is always applied. A `Text` nested inside a coloured `Text` does not inherit the parent colour: pass `tone` to match it. Only the size is inherited, and only when `variant` and `size` are both omitted.

## States

None. The component has no interactive or conditional state.

### Motion

none in source

### Platform notes

none in source

## A11y

- Contrast: Colour is the caller's `tone` on the caller's surface. Reference theme, text tones on raised surfaces: text 17.79/13.83:1, muted 6.16/7.14:1, danger 6.57/7.24:1, accent 5.17/8.86:1, info 6.45/8.17:1, success 5.38/8.72:1, primary 5.81/6.93:1, all above 4.5:1. On sunken surfaces only text, muted and danger are measured (16.01/15.31, 5.54/7.9, 5.91/8.01). onPrimary and onDanger are only meant for filled backgrounds (5.81/7.46:1 and 6.57/8.11:1).
  - UNVERIFIED: tones on surfaces that are not in the contrast table (info, success, accent on sunken) and any consumer theme override (GU3).
- Keyboard and focus: Not interactive.
- Touch target: Not interactive.
- Screen reader: React Native `Text` is read as text. Sets no role. All `accessibility*` props pass through.
  - UNVERIFIED: how a fixed `lineHeight` behaves under the system font scale on each host.
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. The ratios above are arithmetic on the reference theme, but the surface is the caller's and the font-scale behaviour needs a render.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=LayoutText
import { Stack } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Stack";
import { Text } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/layout/Text";

export const Example = () => (
  <Stack gap={1}>
    <Text variant="body">Last sync 09:41</Text>
    <Text variant="caption" tone="muted">Synced 3 devices</Text>
    <Text size={13} tone="danger">Upload failed</Text>
  </Stack>
);
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pick `variant` `caption` for secondary lines, since it is `font[11]` with `leading[14]`.
- Use `tone` `muted` for supporting text, which maps to `text-text-muted` at 6.16/7.14:1 on raised surfaces.
- Pass `size` for a one-off size such as `13`; it replaces the variant and drops the line height.

### Don't

- Do not look for bold or a heading style, because `Text` sets no `fontWeight` and no `fontFamily`; pass them in `style`.
- Do not use `onPrimary` or `onDanger` on a plain surface; they are meant for filled backgrounds only.
- Do not assume a fixed `lineHeight` suits large system font sizes, because the page marks that UNVERIFIED.

# CollapsibleDrawer

## Purpose

Side navigation drawer menu in expanded, compact or minimal mode, with overlay and scrim when open, for React Native; Android back.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/navigation/CollapsibleDrawer
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:

### Dependencies

- `react-native`: `BackHandler`, `Pressable`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `View`, `ViewProps`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (navigation)

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |

| `open` | `boolean` | none | yes | Controlled. |

### Tokens

- `color.primary` (x1), `color.onPrimary` (x1), `color.text` (x1), `color.surfaceRaised` (x1), `color.border` (x1)
- `radius.control` (x1; the file has two `rounded-control` uses)
- `minWidth: 0`, `minHeight: 56`: no token

Tailwind default classes (no token): `h-12`, `w-12`, `rounded-control` (x2), `min-h-11`, `gap-3`, `px-3`, `opacity-40`, `text-sm`, `border` (x3), `border-r`, `flex-row`, `flex-col`, `items-center`, `justify-center`. Unmapped literals: `rgba(0,0,0,0.25)` scrim, `width: 36`, `zIndex` 2 and 3.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: screen reader output for the modal pane, hidden content and toggle; no assistive technology was run.

## Variants

`mode` through `drawerGeometry`:
- `expanded`: pane width `expandedWidth`, labels shown, no overlay, no scrim, content inset `expandedWidth`.
- `compact`: content inset `compactWidth`; pane is `compactWidth` closed, `expandedWidth` open; labels, overlay and scrim only when open.
- `minimal`: content inset 0; pane hidden when closed, `expandedWidth` when open; labels, overlay and scrim only when open. A floating toggle shows while closed.
- The toggle button is not drawn in `expanded`.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `open overlay (compact or minimal with open)` | derived in code | scrim `Pressable` labelled "Close navigation menu"; pane has `accessibilityViewIsModal`; content gets `accessibilityElementsHidden` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"`; Android back closes it; choosing an item closes it. |
| `hidden pane` | class `display: "none"` | `pointerEvents="none"`, `display: "none"`, hidden from accessibility. |
| `selected item` | derived in code | `accessibilityState.selected`; `bg-primary` and `text-on-primary` (styled), plus `selectedItemClassName`. |
| `disabled item` | derived in code | `disabled`, `accessibilityState.disabled`, `opacity-40`. |
| `toggle` | derived in code | label "Close navigation" or "Open navigation", `accessibilityState.expanded` equals the overlay flag. |

No hover, focus, loading or error code.

### Motion

none in source. Pane width and display switch without animation.

### Platform notes

- `BackHandler` `hardwareBackPress` listener while the overlay is open (RN `BackHandler`; behaviour is Android's hardware back).
- Root style `direction: "ltr"` keeps the pane on the physical left in RTL languages (code comment).
- `drawer-model.ts` and the doc comment call it a Windows-compatible fallback that is not WinUI `NavigationView`. No `Platform.OS` checks.

## A11y

- Contrast: Selected item bg-primary with text-on-primary 5.81/7.46:1; others text-text 17.79/13.83:1. Scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.25) decorative.
- Keyboard and focus: No focus-visible class and no focus state on the toggle (:64-72) or the items (:81-93). Whether the host draws a default outline is not in the source (F10). No Escape handler in the file; the scrim Pressable and the toggle close it. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Toggle h-12 w-12 (:69, 48) passes both. Items min-h-11 (:87, 44, no token); header row minHeight 56 (:149). Android items: 44 literal, 4dp under the 48dp Android guideline. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: Toggle: button, label flips Open or Close navigation, state expanded. Items: button, label, state selected and disabled. Content behind an open overlay gets accessibilityElementsHidden and no-hide-descendants (:120-121), pane gets accessibilityViewIsModal (:136). The two lists carry labels but no landmark role (S1).
- Motion: No animation in the file (display toggles).
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. No explicit focus style for any control; default outline not checked (F10).
  - UNVERIFIED: Visible focus on toggle and items (F10). Test: Web: Tab to the toggle and each item, screenshot; native Windows and macOS: same with a keyboard.
  - UNVERIFIED: Hidden content stays unfocusable while overlay is open. Test: Web: open the overlay, press Tab, confirm focus stays inside the pane.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=CollapsibleDrawer
import { useState } from "react";
import { Text } from "react-native";
import { CollapsibleDrawer } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/navigation/CollapsibleDrawer";

export const Example = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>("home");
  return (
    <CollapsibleDrawer mode="compact" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}
      title="Studio" selectedId={selected} onSelectionChange={setSelected}
      items={[{ id: "home", label: "Home" }, { id: "files", label: "Files" }]}
      footerItems={[{ id: "settings", label: "Settings", disabled: false }]}>
      <Text>Screen for {selected}</Text>
    </CollapsibleDrawer>
  );
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Give each `DrawerDestination` a `label`, since without `icon` the first letter of the label is shown.
- Pass `expandedWidth` of at least 180 and `compactWidth` between 44 and `expandedWidth`, since other values throw.
- Wire `onOpenChange` to state, because `open` is controlled and the scrim, toggle and item choice all close it through that callback.

### Don't

- Do not pass `compactWidth` below 44 or at or above `expandedWidth`, because it throws a RangeError.
- Do not ship without checking focus on the toggle and `items`, because neither has a focus-visible class and the status is UNVERIFIED (F10).
- Do not assume Tab stays inside the pane when `open` in `compact` or `minimal` mode, because hidden content staying unfocusable is UNVERIFIED.
