# AnchoredPopover

## Purpose

Modal popover placed against an anchor rectangle or trigger element and clamped to usable regions, for React Native; web Tab cycling.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: none

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/overlays/AnchoredPopover
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { AnchoredPopover } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/overlays/AnchoredPopover";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { AnchoredPopover } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/overlays/AnchoredPopover";`

### Dependencies

- `react-native`: `Modal`, `Platform`, `Pressable`, `View`, `useWindowDimensions`.
- `./popover-position.ts` (re-exports `placePopover`, `hasUsableRegion`, `Rect2D` from `@nyc-tron/core/overlays`), `./focus-cycle.ts` (`cycleFocusIndex`), `./focus-restore.ts` (`useRestoreFocus`), `./useTriggerAnchor.ts`, `./measure-anchor.ts` (`windowRegions`), `./anchored-popover-types.ts`, `../styles.ts` (`joinClasses`).
- No optional peers imported directly.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R2 core family (overlays)
Import count: 4

`PopoverProps = PopoverAnchorProps | PopoverTriggerProps`. Exactly one of `anchor` and `trigger` must be set; `isTriggerPopover` throws `TypeError` for both or neither.

Shared (`PopoverBaseProps`, all readonly):

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| scope | string | "popover" | no | Identity token; a change discards the committed state. |
| open | boolean | none | yes | Controlled. |
| onOpenChange | (open: boolean) => void | none | yes | Called with `false` on Escape, backdrop press and Android back; `toggle` calls it with `!open`. |
| accessibilityLabel | string | none | yes | Used as `aria-label` of the dialog. |
| children | ReactNode | none | yes |  |
| width | number | 320 | no | Preferred; clamped by `placePopover`. |
| maxHeight | number | 420 | no | Preferred; clamped. |
| className | string | none | no | Joined onto the surface classes. |
| testID | string | none | no | On the surface. |

Rect form adds `anchor: Rect2D` (required) and `usableRegions: readonly Rect2D[]` (required). Trigger form adds `trigger: ReactNode | ((state: PopoverTriggerState) => ReactNode)` (required) and `usableRegions?` (default: the whole window as one region from `windowRegions`).

`Rect2D` (core overlays): `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, all number. `PopoverTriggerState`: `open: boolean`, `toggle: () => void`, `triggerProps: { accessibilityState: { expanded }, "aria-expanded", "aria-haspopup": "dialog" }`.

### Tokens

`node tokenuse.mjs` output:
- `color.surfaceRaised` via `bg-surface-raised` (x1), `color.border` via `border-border` (x1), `radius.control` via `rounded-control` (x1)

Tailwind default classes (no token): `border` (x3, includes the `border-border` prefix match), `rounded-control`. Unmapped literals: `position:"absolute"` offsets, `overflow:"hidden"`.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: where `placePopover` puts the surface for a given anchor and regions; its body in `@nyc-tron/core/overlays` was not read.
- UNVERIFIED: focus return to the opener (`useRestoreFocus`) and anchor measurement (`useTriggerAnchor`); those files were not read.

## Variants

- Rect form: draws from the given `anchor` and `usableRegions`.
- Trigger form: renders `trigger` in a `collapsable={false}` `View`, measures it on open through `useTriggerAnchor`, and keeps the surface mounted after the first measurement so closing can restore focus.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | derived in code | `Modal visible={open}`. In the trigger form `visible` is `open && measured`. |
| `no usable region` | derived in code | `hasUsableRegion` false gives no position and the component renders `null`. |
| `trigger expanded` | derived in code | `triggerProps` carry `accessibilityState.expanded`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. |
| `guarded callbacks` | derived in code | `close` runs only while open, with the committed token matching, and with a usable region. |

No hover, disabled, loading or error styling.

### Motion

none in source (`animationType="none"`).

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS !== "web"` returns early from the Tab handler: only web gets Tab and Shift+Tab cycling through `querySelectorAll` of tabbable elements. The comment says native hosts own their Tab chain.
- The type docs say `className` is web only.
- The doc comment names `@nyc-tron/expo-controls/NativePopover` as the SwiftUI and Compose variant for iOS and Android; it is not imported.
- `Modal animationType="none"` always, per the comment about the web focus trap while fading.

## A11y

- Contrast: Surface bg-surface-raised with border-border 1.58/1.58:1; content is the caller's.
- Keyboard and focus: Web: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the popover (:56-65), initial focus onShow focusFirst (:81). Escape through Modal onRequestClose. The scrim Close popover Pressable has focusable={false}. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Not a control; scrim covers the screen.
- Screen reader: Modal with accessibilityViewIsModal; surface role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-label (:86). Scrim has accessibilityLabel "Close popover".
- Motion: animationType="none" (:80), no fade.
- Review status: **PASS**. Dialog role, focus trap, Escape and instant open.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=AnchoredPopover
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
import { AnchoredPopover } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/overlays/AnchoredPopover";

export const Example = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <AnchoredPopover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} accessibilityLabel="Filter options"
      width={280}
      trigger={({ toggle, triggerProps }) => (
        <Pressable {...triggerProps} accessibilityRole="button" onPress={toggle}>
          <Text>Filters</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}>
      <Text>Popover content</Text>
    </AnchoredPopover>
  );
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass exactly one of `anchor` or `trigger`, because `isTriggerPopover` throws `TypeError` for both or neither.
- Set `accessibilityLabel` on every popover, since it becomes the `aria-label` of the dialog.
- Spread `triggerProps` onto the trigger element so it carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`.

### Don't

- Don't pass `anchor` without `usableRegions`; the rect form requires both, and with no usable region the component renders `null`.
- Don't state where `placePopover` puts the surface for a given anchor; the page marks that placement `UNVERIFIED`.

none. `unstyled` is the only switch (drops the `rounded-control border border-border bg-surface-raised p-2 gap-2` surface, the scrim colour and row highlight classes).

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `empty search results` | derived in code | a `Text` with `role="status"` and `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` shows `emptyText`. |

- Motion: animationType fade on native, none on web (:101). Not tied to reduce motion (F09).
- Review status: **FAIL**. Keyboard-active option is marked only by a 1.15/1.2:1 tint (2.4.7, 1.4.11); its TextField inherits F03.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Give each `commands` entry a unique `id` matching `/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._:-]*$/`, because `validateCommands` throws on bad or repeated ids.
- Bump `revision` or change `scope` when the command set changes, since both belong to the reset boundary that clears query and active id.

### Don't

- Don't rely on the active option tint as the keyboard focus cue: `bg-primary/10` measures 1.15/1.2:1 and the review status is FAIL (F02).
- Don't pass more than 1000 `commands` or a blank `label`; `validateCommands` throws on every render.
- Don't put the search field forward as accessible by default; the `TextField` boundary is 1.42/1.75:1 (F03).

| `once settled` | derived in code | after a dismiss or select the open token is marked settled, so a second call in the same open does nothing. |
| `no usable region` | derived in code | renders `null`. |
| `Keyboard (onKeyDown on items)` | derived in code | Escape dismisses, Enter, Space and Spacebar select, Tab and arrows cycle, Home and End jump; modifier keys are ignored. |

### Motion

`Modal` fade on non-desktop platforms; none on desktop. No Animated or Reanimated.

### Platform notes

- `desktop = Platform.OS === "web" || String(Platform.OS) === "qnx" || String(Platform.OS) === "marathon"`. On desktop the `Modal` uses `animationType="none"` and `onShow` focuses the first enabled item; elsewhere `"fade"`.
- The doc comment says WinUI, AppKit, SwiftUI and Compose menu adapters are separate.

## A11y

- Contrast: Items text-text 17.79/13.83:1, destructive text-danger 6.57/7.24:1. Focus style is `focus-visible:bg-primary/10` only (:109): 1.15/1.2:1 (F12).
- Keyboard and focus: Arrow-key item navigation through onItemKey (:108); Modal Escape. Items are real focus targets, so a host outline may also draw (not checked). Desktop, QNX and marathon branch at :48 (no fade, keyboard menu). Windows and macOS follow the web or native branch of Platform.OS.
- Touch target: Items minHeight 56 (:110, no token). Passes both.
- Screen reader: role menu with label, items role menuitem with disabled state (:95-105). Scrim label "Dismiss menu".
- Motion: animationType fade on non-desktop (:87), not tied to reduce motion (F09).
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. Only focus cue in source is a 1.15/1.2:1 tint (F12).
  - UNVERIFIED: Whether a host outline draws on the focused menu item (F12). Test: Open a menu in a browser, press ArrowDown, screenshot the focused item; repeat on Windows and QNX.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=CommandPopover
import { useState } from "react";
import { CommandPopover } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/overlays/CommandPopover";

export const Example = () => {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true);
  return (
    <CommandPopover visible={visible} onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}
      onSelect={id => console.log(id)}
      anchor={{ x: 40, y: 40, width: 120, height: 36 }}
      usableRegions={[{ x: 0, y: 0, width: 800, height: 600 }]}
      items={[
        { id: "rename", label: "Rename", description: "Change the file name" },
        { id: "delete", label: "Delete", danger: true },
      ]} />
  );
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Provide `onDismiss` and flip `visible` to false inside it, since it runs on dismissal and after every selection.
- Mark destructive items with `danger` so they use `text-danger`, which measures 6.57/7.24:1.

### Don't

- Don't count on the focused item being visible: the only source cue is `focus-visible:bg-primary/10` at 1.15/1.2:1 (F12), and a host outline is `UNVERIFIED`.
- Don't pass an `anchor` with no matching `usableRegions`; with no usable region it renders `null`.
- Don't expect a second `onSelect` in the same open; the open token is marked settled after the first dismiss or select.

# AdaptiveDock

## Purpose

Dockable panel layout of tabbed and floating panels; merges into one stack below a width and avoids foldable hinges, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: @nyc-tron/core, react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/DragGrabHandle, @nyc-tron/shell/MenuButton, @nyc-tron/shell/PaneSplitter

## Variants

- Layout mode, derived from measured width: wide (width >= `compactBelow`) puts stacks on left, right and bottom edges in nested `PaneSplitter`s; compact (`0 < width < compactBelow`) merges every docked panel into one stack under the workspace in a vertical `PaneSplitter` sized by `layout.compactSize` (default `round(height*0.45)`, min 160 each side).
- `DockEdge`: `"left" | "right" | "bottom"`. Edge minimums are 160 for a dock and 200 for the workspace.
- `DockTarget`: edge or `"floating"`. Drives the options-menu entries ("Move to left dock", "Move to right dock", "Move to bottom dock", "Float").
- `unstyled`: `true` removes every token class listed under Tokens.

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `disabled` prop | `disabled` prop. `change()` drops proposals, tab and title `Pressable`s get `disabled`, tab `accessibilityState.disabled`, `MenuButton` and `DragGrabHandle` get `disabled`, `PaneSplitter`s get `disabled`, tab `tabIndex` becomes -1. |
| `selected tab` | derived in code | `accessibilityState={{selected,disabled}}`, `aria-selected`, `tabIndex` 0 on the selected tab else -1, classes `bg-surface-sunken forced-colors:border-2 forced-colors:border-[Highlight]` and `text-text font-semibold` (unselected: `bg-transparent`, `text-text-muted`). |
| `focus` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | tab class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus`. |
| `dragging a floating panel` | derived in code | `drag` store state; the panel follows the pointer (`drag.rect`) and a drop-target overlay (`border-2 border-focus bg-primary/10`, 20% of the dock) shows for left, right or bottom, `pointerEvents="none"`. |
| `compact` | derived in code | described under Variants. |
| `hover, pressed` | derived in code | no code. |

## Example

```tsx example=AdaptiveDock
import {useState} from "react";
import {Text} from "react-native";
import {AdaptiveDock, type DockLayout, type DockPanel} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/AdaptiveDock";

const panels: readonly DockPanel[] = [
  {id: "layers", title: "Layers", content: <Text>Layer list</Text>},
  {id: "props", title: "Properties", content: <Text>Property list</Text>},
  {id: "notes", title: "Notes", content: <Text>Notes</Text>},
];

export function Example() {
  const [layout, setLayout] = useState<DockLayout>({
    left: {panels: ["layers"], active: "layers", size: 240},
    right: {panels: ["props"], active: "props", size: 280},
    floating: [{id: "notes", rect: {x: 40, y: 40, width: 320, height: 240}}],
  });
  return (
    <AdaptiveDock panels={panels} layout={layout} onLayoutChange={setLayout} editScope="doc-1" compactBelow={600}>
      <Text>Canvas</Text>
    </AdaptiveDock>
  );
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Keep `layout` and `panels` consistent and update `layout` in `onLayoutChange`, because `validateDockLayout` throws on duplicate or unknown panels and empty stacks.
- Set `compactBelow` to the width where side stacks stop fitting, since narrower docks merge all panels into one stack under the workspace.

### Don't

- Don't pass a blank `editScope` or a `revision` string over 512 chars; both throw `RangeError`.
- Don't claim keyboard-only moving of floating panels works; `DragGrabHandle` is not focusable (F14) and the menu route is `UNVERIFIED`.
- Don't count on the selected tab being visible at 3:1; only bold text marks it (F13), `UNVERIFIED`.

## Variants

- `selectionMode`: `"single"` selects with mode `replace` and rows use `accessibilityRole="radio"`; `"multiple"` uses `checkbox` rows, Shift selects a range, Ctrl/Meta or any non-web platform toggles, plain web press replaces, and Ctrl/Cmd+A selects all visible.
- `height`: number gives the list a fixed `height`; `"fill"` gives the root `flex:1, minHeight:0, minWidth:0` and `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"`.
- Sort (internal, `Select`): Name, Newest, Largest; folders always sort first.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `loading` | `loading` prop | `loading` prop; `busy` disables rows, breadcrumb buttons, sort and open button; empty text becomes "Loading assets…". |
| `pending request` | derived in code | `useOwnedAction` pending sets `busy` and shows a "Cancel asset request" button. |
| `error` | `error` prop | `error` prop or the action's error through `ErrorMessage`. |
| `selected` | derived in code | row `aria-checked`, `accessibilityState.checked`, and a "✓" mark; the roving tab stop (`tabIndex` 0) is the first selected visible row, else the first row. |
| `disabled` | derived in code | rows `disabled`, `aria-disabled`, `accessibilityState.disabled` while busy; breadcrumb for the current location is disabled. |
| `empty` | derived in code | "No assets match" when a query is set, else "This location is empty" (or `emptyState`). |
| `focus` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | row class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus`. |
| `hover, pressed` | derived in code | no code. |

## Example

```tsx example=AssetBrowser
import {useState} from "react";
import {AssetBrowser, type AssetEntry, type AssetLocation} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/AssetBrowser";

const entries: readonly AssetEntry[] = [
  {id: "f1", name: "Textures", kind: "folder"},
  {id: "a1", name: "harbor.png", kind: "file", mediaType: "image/png", byteLength: 204800, modifiedMs: 1700000000000},

export function Example() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<readonly string[]>([]);
  return (
    <AssetBrowser locationId="images" revision="r1" entries={entries} path={path} selectedIds={selected}
      selectionMode="multiple" onSelectionChange={setSelected} height="fill"
      onOpen={async (request, signal) => { if (!signal.aborted) console.log(request.entry.id); }}
      onNavigate={(locationId) => { console.log(locationId); }}/>
  );
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Update `revision` whenever `entries` change, because it is sent back as `expectedRevision` in `AssetRequest`.
- Keep `selectedIds` to one id in the default `selectionMode` of `single`, and switch to `multiple` for ranges.

### Don't

- Don't pass a `height` below 44 or a non-finite number; it throws `RangeError`.
- Don't ship the sort and search fields as accessible fields: they inherit the 1.42/1.75:1 boundary from `Select` and `InspectorSearch` (F03, FAIL).
- Don't send more than 20000 `entries` or duplicate ids; the list is validated.

# ContextMenu

## Purpose

Wraps a target to open a command menu on right-click, long-press, keyboard or screen-reader action, for React Native; QNX focus return.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/overlays/CommandPopover

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/shell/ContextMenu
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { ContextMenu } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/ContextMenu";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { ContextMenu } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/ContextMenu";`

### Dependencies

- `../overlays/CommandPopover` (`CommandPopover`, `CommandMenuItem` type), `../overlays/popover-position` (`hasUsableRegion`, `Rect2D`), `./shell-keys` (`shellKey`).
- External: `react`, `react-native` (`Platform`, `Pressable`, `useWindowDimensions`), `zustand` (optional peer). `@nyc-tron/core/overlays` is reached through `CommandPopover`.

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R3 shell core. Import count: 1 (other packages: 1).
Also exported: types `CommandMenuItem`, `ContextMenuProps`, `ContextMenuSource`; functions `isContextMenuKey(key, shift)` (true for `"ContextMenu"` or Shift+`"F10"`) and `pointAnchor(x, y)` (zero-size `Rect2D`; throws `RangeError` for non-finite input).

`ContextMenuProps extends Omit<PressableProps,"children"|"onLongPress"|"onContextMenu">`. Read or overridden from inherited props: `style` (function or object, merged after `{minWidth:44,minHeight:44}`), `onKeyDown` (called after the menu key check), `accessibilityActions` (a "longpress" action is appended while usable), `onAccessibilityAction` (forwarded for actions other than "longpress"), `testID` (menu gets `<testID>-menu`), `disabled`. `onPress` is not read and stays the target's primary press. The rest spreads onto the `Pressable`.

Extends: `Omit<PressableProps, "children" | "onLongPress" | "onContextMenu">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `string` | `"context-menu"` | no | Part of the boundary; changing it closes the menu and cancels pending measurements. |
| `revision` | `string \| number` | `0` | no | Same boundary role. |
| `label` | `string` | none | yes | Menu `accessibilityLabel` is `"Actions for "+label`. |
| `items` | `readonly CommandMenuItem[]` | none | yes |  |
| `onSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | none | yes | Called only for an enabled item present in the committed list. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | none | yes | The target. |
| `onOpen` | `(source: ContextMenuSource) => void` | none | no |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |
| `usableRegions` | `readonly Rect2D[]` | none | no | Default is the whole window from `useWindowDimensions`. |

`CommandMenuItem` (from `@nyc-tron/core/overlays`): `id: string`, `label: string`, `description?: string`, `disabled?: boolean`, `danger?: boolean` (all readonly).

### Tokens

| Token | Replaces | Count |
|---|---|---|
| size.touch | `minWidth: 44`, `minHeight: 44` | 1 each |

No classes in this file.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: `CommandPopover` keyboard, focus-return and placement behaviour on each platform; only its props were read in this task.
- UNVERIFIED: whether the long-press handler and the web `onContextMenu` both fire for one gesture on a given device; the code opens at the last anchor set.
- UNVERIFIED: VoiceOver and TalkBack output of the "Show actions" action and `aria-haspopup` on native.

## Variants

`ContextMenuSource` reports how the menu opened: `"pointer"` (right-click or stylus barrel click via `onContextMenu`), `"long-press"`, `"keyboard"` (Shift+F10 or Menu key), `"assistive"` (the "Show actions" screen-reader action). No visual variants.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `disabled` prop | `disabled` prop on the `Pressable`; also no menu when no item is enabled or no usable region exists (`usable` false). |
| `open` | derived in code | an anchor in the local store renders a `CommandPopover` with `visible`. |
| `usable` | derived in code | `aria-haspopup="menu"` always; `accessibilityHint` "Has actions. Long press, right-click or press Shift F10." only while usable. |
| `hover, pressed, focus, error, loading` | derived in code | no code in this file. |

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

- `String(Platform.OS)==="qnx"` or `"marathon"`: after the menu closes, focus is moved back to the target with `target.current.focus()`.
- `onContextMenu` uses `nativeEvent.clientX/clientY` (web); without finite coordinates the menu opens beside the target.
- Export conditions: `types`, `react-native`, `default`, same file.

## A11y

- Contrast: Delegates to CommandPopover (F12).
- Keyboard and focus: Opens by long press, right-click or Shift+F10 (hint :85); on QNX and marathon it restores focus to the target when the menu closes (:60). Menu items: see CommandPopover.
- Touch target: Target minWidth and minHeight 44 (:104, size.touch). Android: 44 (F08). Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: aria-haspopup=menu, hint "Has actions. Long press, right-click or press Shift F10.", accessibilityActions longpress "Show actions" (:84-86).
- Motion: Via CommandPopover (F09).
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. Its menu is CommandPopover, whose focus cue is a tint (F12).
  - UNVERIFIED: Focus visibility inside the menu (F12). Test: See CommandPopover.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=ContextMenu
import {Text} from "react-native";
import {ContextMenu, type CommandMenuItem} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/ContextMenu";

const items: readonly CommandMenuItem[] = [
  {id: "duplicate", label: "Duplicate"},
  {id: "delete", label: "Delete", danger: true},
];

export function Example() {
  return (
    <ContextMenu label="Harbor photo layer" scope="layer-7" items={items}
      onSelect={(id) => { console.log(id); }} onOpen={(source) => { console.log(source); }}
      onPress={() => { console.log("primary"); }}>
      <Text>Harbor photo</Text>
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `label` to the target's name, because the menu `accessibilityLabel` is built as "Actions for" plus `label`.
- Pass `usableRegions` when the target sits in a constrained pane, since the default is the whole window.

### Don't

- Don't give every item `disabled`; with no enabled item or no usable region the menu never opens.
- Don't assume the menu has a strong focus cue; it delegates to `CommandPopover` and its `focus-visible:bg-primary/10` tint (F12), `UNVERIFIED`.
- Don't claim `longpress` and `onContextMenu` fire once per gesture; the page marks that `UNVERIFIED`.

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `selectionKind` and `appliesTo` together so only items for the current selection show.
- Set `disabledReason` on a blocked item so users get a hint and a visible line instead of an unexplained dead button.

### Don't

- Don't pass `onLayout` and expect it to run; the component sets its own `onLayout` after the spread and overrides it.
- Don't use duplicate or blank item `id` values or more than 1000 `items`; `validateToolbarItems` throws.
- Don't trust the focus ring on a `pressed` item: `ring-focus` and `bg-primary` share one colour (F07), `UNVERIFIED`.

## Example

```tsx example=DocumentTabBar
import {useState} from "react";
import {DocumentTabBar, activeAfterClose, moveDocument, type DocumentTab} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/DocumentTabBar";

export function Example() {
  const [docs, setDocs] = useState<readonly DocumentTab[]>([
    {id: "a", title: "Harbor.png", dirty: true},
    {id: "b", title: "Notes.md"},
  ]);
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string | undefined>("a");
  return (
    <DocumentTabBar documents={docs} activeId={active} onActivate={setActive}
      onClose={(id) => {
        const ids = docs.map(d => d.id);
        setActive(activeAfterClose(ids, id, active));
        setDocs(docs.filter(d => d.id !== id));
      }}
      onReorder={(id, to) => {
        const order = moveDocument(docs.map(d => d.id), id, to);
        setDocs(order.map(i => docs.find(d => d.id === i)!));
      }}/>
  );
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `onClose` and `onReorder` only when you support them, since without them no close button shows and tabs cannot be reordered.
- Set `dirty` on unsaved documents so the label reads "unsaved changes" and the `border-accent` dot appears.

### Don't

- Don't rely on the selected tab styling alone; raised against sunken is 1.11/1.11:1 plus weight (F13), `UNVERIFIED`.
- Don't pass an `activeId` that matches no tab and expect a selection; none is selected and the first tab becomes the web tab stop.
- Don't use more than 1000 `documents` or blank titles; they are rejected.

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Return a `FindResponse` with a `token` and ordered non-overlapping ranges from `onFind`, because `validateFindResponse` fails the action otherwise.

### Don't

- Don't ship the `Find text` and `Replacement text` inputs as meeting contrast; the boundary is 1.42/1.75:1 (1.4.11, F03) and the review status is FAIL.
- Don't expect `initialQuery` to update later; it is read once when the store is created.
- Don't claim the live region announces every state change; the page marks that `UNVERIFIED`.

# FocusAndA11yLayer

## Purpose

Provider exposing reduce-motion, screen-reader, high-contrast and input-modality state plus announcements, on iOS, Android, web and QNX.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native, zustand

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:

### Dependencies

- `./a11y-model` (`initialA11yState`, `modalityAfterKey`, `queueAnnouncement`, types, `motionDuration`).
- External: `react`, `react-native` (`AccessibilityInfo`, `Platform`, `Text`, `View`), `zustand` (optional peer).

## Props

Tier-1 reason: R3 shell core. Import count: 0 (other packages: 0).
Also exported from the same specifier: hooks `useA11yPreferences()` and `useAnnounce()`; function `motionDuration(ms, preferences)`; types `A11yPreferences`, `InputModality`, `Politeness`, `FocusAndA11yLayerProps`. Both hooks throw `Error("<name> needs a FocusAndA11yLayer above it")` outside the layer.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | none | yes |  |
| `initial` | `Partial<A11yPreferences>` | none (all off, modality `"unknown"`) | no | Starting values; the platform overrides them once it reports. |

`A11yPreferences`: `reduceMotion: boolean`, `screenReader: boolean`, `highContrast: boolean`, `inputModality: "keyboard" | "pointer" | "unknown"` (all readonly).

Helpers: `useAnnounce()` returns `(text: string, politeness?: "polite" | "assertive") => void` (default `"polite"`; blank text is ignored). `motionDuration(ms, {reduceMotion})` returns `0` when reduce motion is on and throws `RangeError` for a negative or non-finite `ms`.

### Tokens

none (no literals or classes).

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: what VoiceOver, TalkBack and browsers actually speak for announcements; the code queues text and sets the live-region props only.
- UNVERIFIED: `AccessibilityInfo` method availability and behaviour on QNX and Marathon hosts beyond the error codes the file handles.
- UNVERIFIED: whether `AccessibilityInfo.isHighTextContrastEnabled` and `isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled` exist at runtime on the React Native version in use; the file calls them without a guard.

## Variants

`Politeness`: `"polite"` or `"assertive"`, set per announcement; on web it becomes the `accessibilityLiveRegion` of the hidden announcement text. `InputModality` values come from keydown (navigation keys or modified single keys give `"keyboard"`) and pointerdown (`"pointer"`).

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `reduceMotion, screenReader, highContrast, inputModality` | derived in code | held in a store and read through `useA11yPreferences`. |
| `Announcement` | derived in code | stored with a `seq` that increments so identical text is read again. |
| `read failure (QNX and Marathon only)` | derived in code | an unexpected rejected read is stored and rethrown during render so it reaches an error boundary. Known codes `ERR_QT_ACCESSIBILITY_UNSUPPORTED` and `ERR_QT_ACCESSIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE` are ignored. |

### Motion

none in source. It supplies `motionDuration` and the `reduceMotion` flag for other components.

### Platform notes

- iOS: reads `isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled` and listens to `darkerSystemColorsChanged` for `highContrast`.
- Android, `qnx`, `marathon`: read `isHighTextContrastEnabled` and listen to `highTextContrastChanged`.
- All platforms: reduce motion and screen reader through `AccessibilityInfo`.
- Web: `matchMedia("(forced-colors: active)")` for `highContrast`, `matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")` for `reduceMotion`; `keydown` and `pointerdown` capture listeners write `document.documentElement.dataset.inputModality`; announcements render in a hidden 1 by 1 `View` with an `accessibilityLiveRegion` `Text` and `aria-atomic`. Screen reader detection is not available on web (reports the initial value).
- Non-web: announcements call `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility`.
- Export conditions: `types`, `react-native`, `default`, same file.

## A11y

- Contrast: No visuals.
- Keyboard and focus: Tracks input modality (keyboard or pointer) through capture listeners on web (:111-116).
- Touch target: Not a control.
- Screen reader: Announcements through AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility on iOS and Android and a visually hidden live region on web (:123-137); useA11yPreferences exposes reduceMotion, screenReader, highContrast.
- Motion: Reads reduceMotion from AccessibilityInfo, QNX and web matchMedia (:72-101) and publishes it. No tier 1 component consumes it (F09).
- Review status: **PASS**. Provides announce and preference hooks; web live region present.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=FocusAndA11yLayer
import {Pressable, Text} from "react-native";
import {FocusAndA11yLayer, motionDuration, useA11yPreferences, useAnnounce} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/FocusAndA11yLayer";

function SaveButton() {
  const announce = useAnnounce();
  const prefs = useA11yPreferences();
  const duration = motionDuration(200, prefs);
  return <Pressable onPress={() => announce(`Saved, ${duration} ms fade`, "polite")}><Text>Save</Text></Pressable>;
}

export function Example() {
  return <FocusAndA11yLayer initial={{reduceMotion: false}}><SaveButton/></FocusAndA11yLayer>;
}
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Mount `FocusAndA11yLayer` above any component that calls `useA11yPreferences` or `useAnnounce`, because both throw outside it.
- Wrap animation lengths in `motionDuration` so `reduceMotion` returns `0`.

### Don't

- Don't pass a negative or non-finite value to `motionDuration`; it throws `RangeError`.
- Don't assume `reduceMotion` already changes the library; no tier 1 component consumes it (F09).
- Don't assume what VoiceOver or TalkBack speak for `useAnnounce`; that output is `UNVERIFIED`.

```tsx example=InspectorPanel
import {useState} from "react";
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `scope` explicitly when the selection object is rebuilt each render, since the default is `JSON.stringify(selection)` and a change drops editor drafts.
- Pass `onQueryChange` together with `query` so a selection other than `none` shows `InspectorSearch`.

### Don't

- Don't ship the panel's search as accessible by default; it renders `InspectorSearch` with a 1.42/1.75:1 boundary (F03, FAIL).
- Don't use a blank or over 512 char `title` in a `single` selection, or a `multiple` `count` under 2; both are rejected.
- Don't claim the `region` label is announced; that output is `UNVERIFIED`.

# KeyboardShortcutHUD

## Purpose

Searchable keyboard shortcut list grouped by category, with rebinding and Apple keycaps, for React Native; iOS and Android need a recorder.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/shell/InspectorSearch

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/shell/KeyboardShortcutHUD
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { KeyboardShortcutHUD } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/KeyboardShortcutHUD";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { KeyboardShortcutHUD } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/KeyboardShortcutHUD";`

### Dependencies

- Internal: `../overlays/popover-position.ts` (`placePopover`, `hasUsableRegion`), `../overlays/focus-restore.ts` (`useRestoreFocus`), `../styles.ts` (`joinClasses`), `./InspectorSearch.tsx`, `./inspector-model.ts` (`matchesQuery`), `./shell-keys.ts` (`shellKey`), `./shortcut-model.ts`.
- External: `react`, `react-native` (Modal, Platform, Pressable, ScrollView, Text, View, useWindowDimensions), `zustand` and `zustand/vanilla`.
- Optional peers: `zustand` (optional in package.json peerDependenciesMeta); `@nyc-tron/core` (optional; the overlay helpers re-export from it).

## Props

The file also exports `isApplePlatform()` (a function, not a component), re-exports `bindingFromChord` and `commandForChord`, and re-exports the types `Binding`, `ChordRecorder`, `KeyChord`, `ShortcutCommand`.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `string` | `"shortcuts"` | no | Part of the reset boundary `[scope, revision, visible]`; a change clears query, recording and errors. |
| `revision` | `string \| number` | `0` | no | Same boundary. |
| `usableRegions` | `readonly Rect2D[]` | window rectangle | no | The sheet is placed with `placePopover` (560 by 560, margin 16) inside the first usable region. If `hasUsableRegion` is false the Modal is not visible. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | none | yes | Modal `visible` is `visible && region exists`. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | none | yes | Called by the backdrop, the Close button and Modal `onRequestClose` when nothing is recording. |
| `commands` | `readonly ShortcutCommand[]` | none | yes | Checked by `validateShortcutCommands` on every render. |
| `onRebind` | `(id: string, binding: Binding \| undefined) => void` | none | no | Without it the list is read-only. A conflict calls it twice: first `(conflictId, undefined)`, then `(id, binding)`. |
| `recorder` | `ChordRecorder` | none | no | Hardware key source for iOS and Android. Ignored on web. |
| `apple` | `boolean` | `isApplePlatform()` | no | Selects Apple keycaps and the wording of the modifier error. |
| `title` | `string` | `"Keyboard shortcuts"` | no | Heading text and the Modal `aria-label`. |
| `className` | `string` | none | no | Joined onto the sheet container. |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Drops every class string the component adds. |

`ShortcutCommand` (shortcut-model.ts):
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| id | `string` | yes | |
| label | `string` | yes | |
| group | `string` | no | Section heading. |
| binding | `Binding` (string such as `"Mod+Shift+S"`) | no | Shown as keycaps, or "Not set". |
| defaultBinding | `Binding` | no | "Reset" restores it. |
| keywords | `readonly string[]` | no | Extra search words. |

`ChordRecorder` has one method, `startRecording(onChord): {remove(): void}`. `KeyChord` has `key` and optional `ctrlKey`, `metaKey`, `altKey`, `shiftKey`.

### Tokens

- Colour classes: color.text (9), color.textMuted (5), color.border (3), color.surfaceSunken (3), color.focus (2), color.danger (1), color.primary (1), color.onPrimary (1), color.surfaceRaised (1).
- Radius classes: radius.control (3), radius.card (1).
- Spacing literals: space.0.75 (gap 3, 1), space.0.5 (paddingVertical 2, 1), space.1 (paddingVertical 4 x2, gap 4 x2, paddingTop 4 x1), space.1.5 (gap 6, 1), space.2 (gap 8 x3, paddingTop 8 x2), space.2.5 (paddingHorizontal 10, 1), space.4 (padding 16 x1, paddingHorizontal 16 x3, paddingBottom 16 x1, paddingVertical 16 x1).
- border.1_5 (borderTopWidth 1.5, 2). size.touch (minHeight 44, 2).
- Component-level: HUD.space.1_25 (paddingHorizontal 5, 1).
- no token: minWidth 22 (1), minWidth 140 (1).
- Tailwind default classes (no token): rounded-control, rounded-card, border, border-2, text-xs, text-sm, text-base, min-h-11, min-w-11, px-2, font-semibold, shadow-md.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: screen reader output of the keycap group label and the live-region messages; it depends on the platform accessibility stack.
- UNVERIFIED: behaviour of `InspectorSearch`, `useRestoreFocus` and `placePopover`; read only as call sites.
- UNVERIFIED: whether `@nyc-tron/hardware-keys` (named in a doc comment as a `recorder` source) exists or behaves as described; it was not read.

## Variants

none. `unstyled` is the only styling switch.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | derived in code | list of commands grouped by `group`. |
| `empty (search)` | derived in code | text `No command matches "<query>".` when the filter leaves nothing; the search summary reads "No shortcuts match". |
| `rebindable vs read-only` | derived in code | "Change" and "Reset" buttons render only when `onRebind` is set and (`Platform.OS==="web"` or `recorder` is set). "Reset" renders only when `defaultBinding` differs from `binding`. |
| `recording` | derived in code | the row shows a focusable field with `accessibilityLabel` "Recording a shortcut for <label>. Press the keys, or Escape to cancel." and class `border-2 border-focus` when styled. |
| `error` | derived in code | text in `accessibilityLiveRegion="assertive"`, class `text-danger`, when the binding has no Ctrl, Alt or Command (function keys excepted). |
| `conflict` | derived in code | assertive live-region text naming the other command, with "Replace" and "Cancel" buttons. |
| `hidden` | derived in code | `visible` false, or no usable region. |
| `focus` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` on the small buttons; focus returns through `useRestoreFocus(visible && region)`. |
| `hover` | class `hover:bg-surface-sunken` | `hover:bg-surface-sunken` on the small buttons. |

### Motion

none in source (`Modal animationType="none"`).

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS==="web"`: enables rebinding without `recorder`; recording reads the browser `onKeyDown`; prompt text is "Press the new shortcut, or Esc to cancel".
- iOS and Android: rebinding needs `recorder`; prompt text is "Press the new shortcut on the hardware keyboard, or Esc to cancel"; Escape is read from the recorder chord.
- `isApplePlatform()`: true for `Platform.OS` "ios" or "macos", or when `navigator.platform`/`userAgent` matches `/Mac|iPhone|iPad/`.
- The Modal sets `accessibilityViewIsModal` and `aria-label`; a comment says React Native Web makes the Modal the dialog.
- Package export: `react-native` and `default` conditions both point at `dist/components/shell/KeyboardShortcutHUD.js`.

## A11y

- Contrast: Text text-text 16.01/15.31:1; recording field border-2 border-focus 5.22/7.67:1; errors text-danger 5.91/8.01:1. Renders InspectorSearch (F03).
- Keyboard and focus: Modal; Escape cancels recording or closes (:113-119, :177). Record field focusable with onKeyDown (:157-158). Buttons `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-focus` (focus/surfaceRaised 5.81/6.93:1, focus/surfaceSunken 5.22/7.67:1). Apple versus non-Apple key labels at :49. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Buttons min-h-11 min-w-11 (:140), rows minHeight 44 (:146, :159). Android: 44 (F08). Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: Modal with aria-label and accessibilityViewIsModal; key combos spoken through bindingSpoken; recording prompt and conflicts are assertive live regions; groups have header role (:135-200).
- Motion: animationType="none" (:177).
- Review status: **FAIL**. Renders InspectorSearch (F03).
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=KeyboardShortcutHUD
import {useState} from "react";
import {KeyboardShortcutHUD,type ShortcutCommand} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/KeyboardShortcutHUD";

const initial:ShortcutCommand[]=[
  {id:"save",label:"Save",group:"File",binding:"Mod+S",defaultBinding:"Mod+S"},
  {id:"export",label:"Export",group:"File",binding:"Mod+Shift+E",defaultBinding:"Mod+Shift+E",keywords:["render"]},
];
export const Example=()=>{
  const [visible,setVisible]=useState(true);
  const [commands,setCommands]=useState(initial);
  return <KeyboardShortcutHUD visible={visible} onDismiss={()=>setVisible(false)} commands={commands}
    onRebind={(id,binding)=>setCommands(cs=>cs.map(c=>c.id===id?{...c,binding}:c))}/>;
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `onRebind` to allow changes and a `recorder` on iOS and Android, since rebinding there needs a hardware key source.
- Set `defaultBinding` on each `ShortcutCommand` so Reset appears when `binding` differs.

### Don't

- Don't ship the search as accessible by default; the HUD renders `InspectorSearch` with a 1.42/1.75:1 boundary (F03, FAIL).
- Don't expect `onRebind` to run once on a conflict; it is called twice, first `(conflictId, undefined)`.
- Don't rely on `@nyc-tron/hardware-keys` as a `recorder` source; its existence is `UNVERIFIED`.

# MenuButton

## Purpose

Button that opens a command popover menu; ArrowDown opens it on web, for React Native; QNX focus return.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/overlays/CommandPopover

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/shell/MenuButton
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { MenuButton } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/MenuButton";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { MenuButton } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/MenuButton";`

### Dependencies

- Internal: `../overlays/CommandPopover.tsx` (`CommandPopover`, type `CommandMenuItem`), `../overlays/popover-position.ts`, `../styles.ts`, `./shell-keys.ts`.
- External: `react`, `react-native` (Platform, Pressable, useWindowDimensions), `zustand`, `zustand/vanilla`.
- Optional peers: `zustand`, `@nyc-tron/core`.

## Props

Extends `PressableProps` minus `children`, `onPress`, `accessibilityLabel`, `aria-label`. Other PressableProps are spread onto the Pressable (`{...rest}`) before the component's own props, so `accessibilityRole`, `accessibilityState`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `disabled`, `onPress` and `className` set by the component win. `style` and `testID` are read: `style` is forwarded, `testID` yields `<testID>-popover` on the popover.

Extends: `Omit<PressableProps, "children" | "onPress" | "accessibilityLabel" | "aria-label">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | none | yes | Becomes `accessibilityLabel` and the popover label. |
| `editScope` | `string` | `"menu"` | no | Throws `RangeError` if blank or over 32768 characters. A change closes the menu. |
| `items` | `readonly CommandMenuItem[]` | none | yes |  |
| `onSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | none | yes | Called only for an enabled item while the menu is still owned. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | none | yes | Button content. |
| `usableRegions` | `readonly Rect2D[]` | window rectangle | no |  |
| `menuWidth` | `number` | `240` | no | Passed as `width` to `CommandPopover`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Also disabled when no item is enabled or no usable region exists. |
| `className` | `string` | none | no | Appended last to the class list. |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Drops `rounded-control` and the focus ring. |
| `ref` | `Ref<ComponentRef<typeof Pressable>>` | none | no | Function or object ref is filled with the Pressable node. |

`CommandMenuItem` (core/overlays.ts): `{id: string; label: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; danger?: boolean}`.

### Tokens

- color.focus (1), radius.control (1).
- Tailwind default classes (no token): min-h-11, min-w-11, rounded-control, opacity-40.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: popover placement, dismissal and focus handling outside qnx/marathon; they live in `CommandPopover`, which was not read.
- UNVERIFIED: whether `measureInWindow` exists on every target; the code skips opening if it is missing.

## Variants

none.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `default` | derived in code | closed button. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` prop | `accessibilityState.disabled` is true and `disabled` is passed to Pressable when `disabled`, no enabled item, or no usable region; class `opacity-40`. |
| `expanded` | derived in code | `aria-expanded` and `accessibilityState.expanded` are true while the popover is open. |
| `focus` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` when styled. |
| `opening` | derived in code | `onPress` and ArrowDown (without Alt, Ctrl, Meta) measure the button with `measureInWindow` and open the popover only if width and height are positive. |

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

- When the popover closes, focus returns to the button explicitly only if `String(Platform.OS)` is `"qnx"` or `"marathon"`. Other platforms rely on whatever `CommandPopover` does.
- ArrowDown opening is attached through `onKeyDown`, which React Native delivers on web.
- Package export: `react-native` and `default` conditions both point at `dist/components/shell/MenuButton.js`.

## A11y

- Contrast: Opens CommandPopover (F12). Disabled opacity 0.4 exempt.
- Keyboard and focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-focus` (focus/surfaceRaised 5.81/6.93:1, focus/surfaceSunken 5.22/7.67:1) (:89). ArrowDown opens the menu (:84-86); on QNX and marathon focus returns to the button on close (:73). Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: min-h-11 min-w-11 (:88, 44). Android: 44 literal, 4dp under the 48dp Android guideline. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: role=button, label, aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded, state expanded and disabled (:80-82).
- Motion: Via CommandPopover (F09).
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. Menu is CommandPopover (F12).
  - UNVERIFIED: Focus visibility inside the opened menu (F12). Test: See CommandPopover.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=MenuButton
import {Text} from "react-native";
import {MenuButton} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/MenuButton";

export const Example=()=><MenuButton label="Panel options" items={[
  {id:"rename",label:"Rename"},
  {id:"delete",label:"Delete",danger:true},
]} onSelect={id=>console.log(id)}><Text>Options</Text></MenuButton>;
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `label` on every `MenuButton`, because it becomes the `accessibilityLabel` and the popover label.
- Give at least one enabled entry in `items`, since the button disables itself when none is enabled.

### Don't

- Don't pass a blank `editScope` or one over 32768 characters; it throws `RangeError`.
- Don't count on a visible focus cue inside the menu; `CommandPopover` uses a 1.15/1.2:1 tint (F12), and a host outline is `UNVERIFIED`.
- Don't expect focus to return to the button on every platform; the page says it is explicit only when `Platform.OS` is `qnx` or `marathon`.

# PaneSplitter

## Purpose

Two-pane splitter, horizontal or vertical, resizable by drag, keys or accessibility actions, fold-aware, for React Native and web.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: @nyc-tron/core, react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/gestures/PanResponderDrag

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/shell/PaneSplitter
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { PaneSplitter } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/PaneSplitter";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { PaneSplitter } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/PaneSplitter";`

### Dependencies

- Internal: `../gestures/drag-controller.ts`, `../gestures/drag-transport.ts`, `../gestures/PanResponderDrag.tsx`, `../styles.ts`, `./shell-keys.ts`, `./splitter-model.ts`.
- External: `react`, `react-native`, `zustand`, `zustand/vanilla`, `@nyc-tron/core/folds` (types `FoldFeature`, `Rect`).
- Optional peers: `zustand`, `@nyc-tron/core`.

## Props

Also exports the type `SplitAxis` (`"horizontal" | "vertical"`).

Extends `ViewProps` minus `children`. Read or forwarded specially: `style` (merged into the root style array), `onLayout` (called after the component stores its size). Remaining ViewProps spread onto the root View.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `editScope` | `string` | none | no | Throws `RangeError` if blank or over 16384 characters. Part of the interaction scope; a change cancels a drag. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |
| `axis` | `SplitAxis` | none | yes | `horizontal`: panes side by side. `vertical`: stacked. |
| `start` | `ReactNode` | none | yes |  |
| `end` | `ReactNode` | none | yes |  |
| `size` | `number` | none | yes | Controlled size in points of the pane named by `sizeEdge`. |
| `sizeEdge` | `"start" \| "end"` | `"start"` | no |  |
| `onPreview` | `(size: number) => void` | none | no | During drag; also called with the committed `size` on cancel. |
| `onCommit` | `(size: number) => void` | none | yes | Once per drag, keyboard step, jump or accessibility action. |
| `minStart` | `number` | `120` | no | Must be finite and not negative. |
| `minEnd` | `number` | `120` | no | Same. |
| `label` | `string` | none | yes | `accessibilityLabel` of the divider. |
| `features` | `readonly FoldFeature[]` | `[]` | no | Hinge features in window space. |
| `container` | `Rect` | measured | no | Window-space bounds; if omitted and features exist, the component calls `measureInWindow`. |
| `isRTL` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Horizontal only: start pane is physically on the right. |
| `keyboardStep` | `number` | `16` | no | Must be above 0. |
| `dividerSize` | `number` | `9` | no | Not negative. Divider thickness off a hinge. |
| `transport` | `DragTransport` | `PanResponderDrag` | no | Component type receiving `onBegin`, `onMove`, `onRelease`, `onCancel`, `disabled`. |
| `className` | `string` | none | no | Root; also `min-h-0 min-w-0`. |
| `startClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `endClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `dividerClassName` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |

Non-finite `size`, `minStart`, `minEnd`, `keyboardStep` or `dividerSize` also throw `RangeError`. `FoldFeature` (core/folds.ts): `bounds: Rect`, `orientation: "vertical" | "horizontal"`, `separating: boolean`, `occlusion: "none" | "full"`. `Rect`: `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`.

### Tokens

- color.accent (1), color.focus (1), color.border (1), color.surfaceSunken (1).
- Component-level: PaneSplitter.space.n5_5 (marginLeft -22, marginTop -22).
- no token: minWidth 0, minHeight 0, divider widths 9, 44 and 3 / 1, margins -1.5 / -0.5, `DRAG_SNAP` 24.
- Tailwind default classes (no token): border, min-h-0, min-w-0.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: hinge seating and snap results; they come from `splitter-model.ts`, which was not read.
- UNVERIFIED: how `PanResponderDrag` distinguishes touch from mouse and how many pointers it reports.
- UNVERIFIED: screen reader announcements for `aria-valuetext` ("<n> points") and the adjustable role.

## Variants

- `axis`: `horizontal` sets pane width and a vertical divider line (`borderLeftWidth`); `vertical` sets pane height and a horizontal line (`borderTopWidth`); root `flexDirection` is `row` or `column`.
- `sizeEdge`: chooses which pane `size` measures; `onPreview`/`onCommit` report in the same edge.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `dragging` | derived in code | preview layout set; divider class `border-accent`, line 3 wide. |
| `focused` | derived in code | divider class `border-focus`, line 3 wide. |
| `seated on a hinge` | derived in code | divider class `bg-surface-sunken` when styled. |
| `idle` | derived in code | `border-border`, line 1 wide. |

- default, disabled (`accessibilityState.disabled`, `aria-disabled`, no accessibility actions, `focusable` false, `tabIndex` -1 on web).
- before the first layout measurement, no panes render.

### Motion

none in source. A drag snaps within `DRAG_SNAP` (24) of a hinge band.

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS==="web"`: divider gets `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation`, `focusable`, `tabIndex`, `onKeyDown`; `userSelect: "none"` and `cursor` (`col-resize` or `row-resize`) styles apply.
- Other platforms: divider gets `accessibilityRole="adjustable"`; adjustment is through `increment` and `decrement` accessibility actions ("Grow first pane", "Shrink first pane").
- Keys on web: arrows step (direction swaps in RTL), Home and End jump to limits, Escape cancels a drag; events with Alt, Ctrl or Meta are ignored.
- Package export: `react-native` and `default` conditions both point at `dist/components/shell/PaneSplitter.js`.

## A11y

- Contrast: Idle divider is a 1px border-border line 1.42/1.75:1; hover or drag turns it border-accent 4.65/9.81:1, focus border-focus 5.22/7.67:1 at 3px (:191-199). The idle line is the only visible cue (F06).
- Keyboard and focus: Web: role=separator, focusable, tabIndex 0, arrow keys (:206-213). Native: accessibilityRole=adjustable. State-driven focus line, so no class dependency. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Hit area 44pt across the divider (:222-223, size.touch). Android: 44 (F08). Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: role=separator or adjustable, label, hint, aria-valuemin/max/now/text, increment and decrement actions (:206-213).
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **FAIL**. Idle divider 1.42/1.75:1 is the only visible cue (1.4.11, minor).
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=PaneSplitter
import {useState} from "react";
import {Text} from "react-native";
import {PaneSplitter} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/PaneSplitter";

export const Example=()=>{
  const [size,setSize]=useState(240);
  return <PaneSplitter axis="horizontal" label="Resize layers panel" size={size} onCommit={setSize}
    start={<Text>Layers</Text>} end={<Text>Canvas</Text>}/>;
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass a non-blank `label`; it becomes the divider's `accessibilityLabel` and the only name a screen reader gets for the handle.
- Update `size` from `onCommit`, which fires once per drag, keyboard step, jump or accessibility action, and use `onPreview` for live feedback during the drag.
- Set `isRTL` when the start pane sits on the right in a horizontal splitter, so the arrow-key direction swaps to match.

### Don't

- Do not pass a blank or non-finite `editScope`, `size`, `minStart`, `minEnd` or `keyboardStep`; each throws a `RangeError`.
- Do not rely on the idle divider as the only cue; the 1px `color.border` line measures 1.42/1.75:1 and fails the a11y review (F06).
- Do not assume hinge snapping or screen reader announcements of `aria-valuetext` work; the page marks both UNVERIFIED.

## Variants

- `filter`: `all` shows every preset; `favorites` passes the list through `filterPresets`. The empty favorites view shows "No favorite presets yet." and "Use the bookmark on a preset to keep it here."; the empty all view shows "No presets.".

## States

|---|---|---|

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS==="web"`: tiles get `onKeyDown` and `tabIndex` (0 for one tile, -1 for others), so the grid is one Tab stop with arrow, Home and End movement.
- RTL: arrow direction flips when `nodeIsRTL(target)` or `I18nManager.isRTL`.
- Pointer hover uses `onHoverIn` and `onHoverOut`; focus and blur also drive `onPreview` on all platforms.
- Package export: `react-native` and `default` conditions both point at `dist/components/shell/PresetGallery.js`.

## A11y

- Contrast: Selected tile border-2 border-focus with bg-primary/10 5.81/6.93:1; text-text 17.79/13.83:1; favourite glyph border-accent 5.17/8.86:1.

Focusing a tile previews the preset in the host (:118) (F18). Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Tiles min-h-11, filter and favourite buttons min-h-11 min-w-11 (:97, :120, :133). Android: 44 literal, 4dp under the 48dp Android guideline. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: radiogroup of role=radio tiles with checked state; filter buttons with aria-pressed; favourite toggles with composed labels (:95-131).
- Motion: None.

## Example

```tsx example=PresetGallery
import {useState} from "react";
import {View} from "react-native";
import {PresetGallery,type Preset,type PresetFilter} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/PresetGallery";

const swatch=(c:string)=><View style={{flex:1,backgroundColor:c}}/>;
const presets:Preset[]=[
  {id:"warm",name:"Warm",preview:swatch("#c96")},
  {id:"cool",name:"Cool",preview:swatch("#69c"),favorite:true},
];
export const Example=()=>{
  const [selected,setSelected]=useState<string|undefined>("warm");
  const [filter,setFilter]=useState<PresetFilter>("all");
  return <PresetGallery label="Color grade presets" presets={presets} selectedId={selected} onSelect={setSelected}
    onFavoriteChange={(id,fav)=>console.log(id,fav)} filter={filter} onFilterChange={setFilter}/>;
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass both `onFavoriteChange` and `onFilterChange` when you want the All and Favorites buttons, since they render only when both are set.
- Treat `onPreview` as hover and focus feedback and make it side-effect light, because it also fires on focus (F18).
- Set `label` to a descriptive name; it names the radiogroup and the filter group is named `<label> filter`.

### Don't

- Do not claim focus-driven `onPreview` is accessible without a screen reader test; whether it counts as a change of context is UNVERIFIED (F18).
- Do not assume the column count or arrow-key target math; `galleryColumns` and `gridFocusTarget` were not read and are UNVERIFIED.
- Do not omit `selectedId`, `onSelect` or `presets`; they are required props, and `presets` is checked by `validatePresets`.

## Example

```tsx example=PropertyRow
import {Text} from "react-native";
import {PropertyRow} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/PropertyRow";

export const Example=()=><PropertyRow label="Opacity" override="overridden" onRevert={()=>{}} keywords={["alpha"]}>
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Pass `mixed` when the selection holds differing values; it shows a Mixed badge and adds ', mixed values' to `editorLabel`.
- Set `override="overridden"` together with `onRevert` to get the Revert button, which is labelled 'Revert {label}' and has a 44pt target.
- Use the render-function form of `children` and apply the `PropertyEditorState` fields (`disabled`, `mixed`, `editorLabel`) to your editor.

### Don't

- Do not pass a blank `label` or one over 512 characters; it throws a `RangeError`.
- Do not give `keywords` more than 256 entries or entries over 512 characters, since either throws a `RangeError`.
- Do not expect Revert to show with only `override="overridden"`; without `onRevert` the button is absent and only the hidden dot marks the state.

### Platform notes

## Example

```tsx example=RangeSlider
import {useState} from "react";
import {RangeSlider,type RangeValue} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/RangeSlider";

export const Example=()=>{
  const [value,setValue]=useState<RangeValue>([20,80]);
  return <RangeSlider label="Opacity range" min={0} max={100} step={1} minGap={5} unit="%" value={value} onCommit={setValue}/>;

```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Set `min`, `max` and `step` with `max > min` and `step > 0`; `assertRange` throws otherwise.
- Use `thumbLabels` to give each thumb a distinct name, since thumb names are `<label> <thumbLabel>` and default to Minimum and Maximum.
- Pass `context` when users should type endpoints with units; `unit` alone is only appended to `aria-valuetext`.

### Don't

- Do not ship it as accessible yet; it renders `UnitInput`, whose field boundary is 1.42/1.75:1 (F03), and the page status is FAIL.
- Do not rely on the unfilled track as a visible cue; its `color.border` contrast is 1.42/1.75:1 and still unverified by measurement (F15).
- Do not pass a blank `label` or `scope`, or a non-finite range, because each throws a `RangeError`.

# RibbonTabs

## Purpose

Office-style ribbon of tabs and a command panel of buttons, split buttons and galleries; collapsible, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native
- Requires: @nyc-tron/shell/MenuButton, @nyc-tron/shell/SplitButton

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/shell/RibbonTabs
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { RibbonTabs } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/RibbonTabs";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { RibbonTabs } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/RibbonTabs";`

### Dependencies

- Internal: `../overlays/popover-position.ts` (type), `../styles.ts`, `./MenuButton.tsx`, `./SplitButton.tsx`, `./shell-keys.ts`, `./ribbon-model.ts`.
- External: `react`, `react-native` (I18nManager, Platform, Pressable, ScrollView, Text, View).
- Optional peers: none for this file directly; `MenuButton` pulls in `zustand` (optional peer).

## Props

Exports one component, `RibbonTabs`, plus the type `RibbonTabsProps` and type re-exports `RibbonButton`, `RibbonCommand`, `RibbonGallery`, `RibbonGalleryItem`, `RibbonGroup`, `RibbonSplit`, `RibbonTab`. The inner `Gallery` component is not exported.

Extends `ViewProps` minus `children`. `style` is forwarded to the root; others spread onto it.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `string` | `"ribbon"` | no | Boundary is `[scope, revision, disabled, active tab id, collapsed]`. |
| `revision` | `string \| number` | `0` | no |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |
| `tabs` | `readonly RibbonTab[]` | none | yes | `validateRibbon` throws on over 64 tabs, duplicate ids, empty labels or an invalid gallery selection. |
| `activeTabId` | `string` | none | yes | Falls back to the first tab if it matches none. |
| `onTabChange` | `(id: string) => void` | none | yes |  |
| `onCommand` | `(commandId: string, itemId?: string) => void` | none | yes | `itemId` is set for split flyout and gallery picks. |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | `false` | no | Hides the command panel. |
| `onCollapsedChange` | `(collapsed: boolean) => void` | none | no | The collapse chevron renders only when set. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Ribbon"` | no | Name of the tab list. |
| `usableRegions` | `readonly Rect2D[]` | none | no | Passed to split flyouts and the gallery "More" menu. |
| `className` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `unstyled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |

Model types, one level: `RibbonTab {id, label, contextualGroup?, groups: RibbonGroup[]}`; `RibbonGroup {id, label, commands: RibbonCommand[]}`; `RibbonButton {kind:"button", id, label, icon?, pressed?, disabled?}`; `RibbonSplit {kind:"split", id, label, icon?, items: CommandMenuItem[], disabled?}`; `RibbonGallery {kind:"gallery", id, label, items: RibbonGalleryItem[], selectedId?, inline? (default 4 per doc comment)}`; `RibbonGalleryItem {id, label, preview: ReactNode}`.

### Tokens

- Colour classes: color.focus (6), color.textMuted (4), color.primary (3), color.border (3), color.surfaceSunken (2), color.text (2), color.accent (2), color.surfaceRaised (1).
- radius.control (3).
- Spacing: space.0.5 (gap 2 x3, paddingTop 2 x1), space.1 (paddingHorizontal 4, padding 4, gap 4 x3, marginVertical 4), space.3 (paddingHorizontal 12), space.1.5 (paddingHorizontal 6).
- border.1_5 (borderRightWidth, borderBottomWidth), border.1 (borderLeftWidth).
- no token: tab rule height 3, chevron size 8.
- Tailwind default classes (no token): min-h-11, min-w-11, gap-2, px-2, px-3, rounded-control, border, opacity-40, text-sm, text-xs, font-semibold.

### Unverified

- UNVERIFIED: `rovingTarget` return values for each key; `shell-keys.ts` was not read.
- UNVERIFIED: screen reader output for `tablist`, `tab` and `tabpanel` roles on native.
- UNVERIFIED: how many inline gallery items show (`inlineGalleryItems` was not read; the default 4 is from a doc comment).

## Variants

- Command `kind`: `button` renders a Pressable, a toggle when `pressed` is defined; `split` renders a `SplitButton`; `gallery` renders inline radio items plus a "More" `MenuButton` when `items.length` exceeds the inline count.
- `contextualGroup` on a tab: shows the group name above the tab in `text-accent` and gives the tab `border-t-2 border-accent`.

## States

| State | How it is set | What the code does |
|---|---|---|
| `tab selected` | derived in code | `accessibilityState.selected` and `aria-selected` true only when the tab is active and the panel is not collapsed; label `text-text font-semibold`, 3-wide `border-primary` rule. |
| `tab roving focus` | derived in code | web `tabIndex` 0 on the selected tab, -1 on the rest. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` prop | `disabled` on tabs and commands; per-command `disabled` adds `opacity-40`. |
| `toggle pressed` | derived in code | `aria-pressed`, `accessibilityState.selected`, classes `bg-primary/10 border border-focus`. |
| `collapsed` | `collapsed` prop | panel not rendered; collapse button has `aria-expanded`, label "Show ribbon commands" or "Hide ribbon commands". Picking a tab while collapsed calls `onCollapsedChange(false)`. |
| `gallery item` | derived in code | `role="radio"`, `aria-checked`, classes `border border-focus bg-primary/10` when selected. |
| `focus and hover` | class `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus` | `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-focus`, `hover:bg-surface-sunken`. |

### Motion

none in source.

### Platform notes

- `Platform.OS==="web"`: tabs and gallery items get `onKeyDown` and `tabIndex`; arrow keys move focus and also select the tab (or gallery item) through `rovingTarget`.
- RTL: `nodeIsRTL(target)` or `I18nManager.isRTL` passed to `rovingTarget`.
- Tab list and panel scroll horizontally with `ScrollView` on all platforms.
- Package export: `react-native` and `default` conditions both point at `dist/components/shell/RibbonTabs.js`.

## A11y

- Contrast: Selected tab text-text semibold with a 3px border-primary top bar 5.81/6.93:1; pressed commands bg-primary/10 plus border-focus 5.81/6.93:1; text-accent 5.17/8.86:1; inactive text-text-muted 6.16/7.14:1.
- Keyboard and focus: Web: roving tabIndex and arrows (:58, :97); `focus-visible:ring-2 ring-focus` (focus/surfaceRaised 5.81/6.93:1, focus/surfaceSunken 5.22/7.67:1). Commands inside use MenuButton and SplitButton. Windows, macOS, QNX: no Platform.OS branch in the file, focus visuals are the host's (GU1).
- Touch target: Tabs min-h-11, commands min-h-11 min-w-11 (:78, :98, :112). Android: 44 literal, 4dp under the 48dp Android guideline. Android 48dp: below (F08).
- Screen reader: tablist, tab with selected state, tabpanel with label, groups, toggles with aria-pressed, gallery as radiogroup with radio items (:75-143).
- Motion: None.
- Review status: **UNVERIFIED**. Embeds MenuButton and SplitButton menus (F12).
  - UNVERIFIED: Focus visibility inside ribbon menus (F12). Test: See CommandPopover.
- Reviewed from source only. Nothing was rendered and no screen reader was run. See `docs/agent-native/05-accessibility-review.md`.

## Example

```tsx example=RibbonTabs
import {useState} from "react";
import {RibbonTabs,type RibbonTab} from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/RibbonTabs";

const tabs:RibbonTab[]=[
  {id:"home",label:"Home",groups:[{id:"clip",label:"Clipboard",commands:[
    {kind:"button",id:"paste",label:"Paste"},
    {kind:"button",id:"bold",label:"Bold",pressed:false},
    {kind:"split",id:"export",label:"Export",items:[{id:"pdf",label:"PDF"},{id:"png",label:"PNG"}]},
  ]}]},
  {id:"insert",label:"Insert",groups:[]},
];
export const Example=()=>{
  const [active,setActive]=useState("home");
  const [collapsed,setCollapsed]=useState(false);
  return <RibbonTabs tabs={tabs} activeTabId={active} onTabChange={setActive} onCommand={(id,item)=>console.log(id,item)}
    collapsed={collapsed} onCollapsedChange={setCollapsed}/>;
};
```

## Do/Don't

### Do

- Give every tab in `tabs` a unique `id` and non-empty label; `validateRibbon` throws on duplicates, empty labels or more than 64 tabs.
- Pass `onCollapsedChange` if users should collapse the ribbon, because the chevron renders only when it is set.
- Read `itemId` in `onCommand` to tell split flyout and gallery picks apart from plain button presses.

### Don't

- Do not assume menu focus is visible; focus inside the `SplitButton` and `MenuButton` menus is UNVERIFIED (F12).
- Do not pick a `selectedId` that is not in a gallery's `items`; `validateRibbon` rejects an invalid gallery selection.
- Do not rely on the inline gallery count of 4; it comes from a doc comment and `inlineGalleryItems` is UNVERIFIED.

# RotaryKnob

## Purpose

Dial control with relative or circular drag, fine adjustment, detents and reset to default, for React Native.

## Install

- Package: @nyc-tron/ui
- Peers: react, react-native, zustand
- Requires: @nyc-tron/gestures/PanResponderDrag, @nyc-tron/shell/UnitInput

### Registry install

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add @nyc-tron/shell/RotaryKnob
```

After a registry install, import from the installed path. `shadcn add` rewrites the `@/components` and `@/lib` prefixes to the aliases in the app's `components.json`.
- Import: `import { RotaryKnob } from "@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/RotaryKnob";`

### Tarball install

Install @nyc-tron/ui from the release tarball (README, "Installing from a release"), then import from the package:
- Import: `import { RotaryKnob } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/shell/RotaryKnob";`

### Dependencies

- Internal: `../forge/inputs/precision.ts`, `../gestures/*`, `../styles.ts`, `./shell-keys.ts`, `./slider-model.ts`, `./UnitInput.tsx`, `./unit-expression.ts`.
- External: `react`, `react-native`, `zustand`, `zustand/vanilla`.
- Optional peers: `zustand`.

## Props

Also exports types `KnobInput` (`"relative" | "circular"`) and `RotaryKnobProps`.

Extends `ViewProps` minus `children`, and `RangeConfig`. `style` is merged after the opacity style.

Extends: `Omit<ViewProps, "children">, RangeConfig`

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `string` | `"RotaryKnob"` | no |  |
| `revision` | `string \| number` | `0` | no |  |
| `label` | `string` | none | yes | Blank throws. |
| `value` | `number` | none | yes | Must be finite. |
| `onPreview` | `(value: number) => void` | none | no |  |
| `onCommit` | `(value: number) => void` | none | yes |  |
| `input` | `KnobInput` | `"relative"` | no | Any other value throws. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | none | no | Must be finite and within min and max. Reset button shows when it differs from `value`. |
| `unit` | `string` | none | no |  |
| `context` | `UnitContext` | none | no |  |
| `size` | `number` | `72` | no | Must be finite, above 0 and at most 4096. Dial is `max(44, size)`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | no |  |

### Inherited props this component reads

Documented by hand from the source. They come from the extended type, so they are not in the table above.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
